#4400. Check your ego at the door: Stellantis’ new electric dolly turns ANY car into a tow rig

We all know the type: grizzled stubble, wraparound PitVipers, a MAGA hat quietly retired after last week’s deep-blue shellacking, and a pristine, polished pickup parked in the driveway that they “need for towing.” With Stellantis’ new patent for an AI-powered electric tow dolly that turns just about ANY vehicle into a capable tow rig, however, those might need a new to find a new excuse to keep that gas-guzzler.

Originally filed in 2023, Stellantis received US Patent No. 12,779,916 for its electric tow dolly on 03NOV2026. The patent covers a machine that’s designed to shoulder the trailer’s hitch load with its own ball hitch or fifth-wheel plate, using an on-board electric motor and battery to get the trailer going while its regenerative braking system and AI-backed steering and traction control system keeps everything pointed in the right direction.

In other words, the dolly takes on many of the jobs that traditionally require a big tow vehicle: providing the pulling power, managing the trailer’s weight and controlling its braking and traction. The vehicle up front doesn’t necessarily need a massive motor, heavy-duty suspension or oversized brakes. With a system like this, you could argue that the “tow vehicle” isn’t really a tow vehicle at all. It’s more of a “lead vehicle,” since the dolly is the one doing the towing … and it can follow just about anything – including the diminutive (and supremely affordable) Fiat 500e, which is also made by Stellantis.

To be clear, this isn’t just Uncle Jojo making fun of the commuter conveys – Stellantis’ patent describes the dolly as being equipped with an autonomous control system using cameras, sensors, a controller, and an advanced, four wheel steer-by-wire system. It also specifically discusses how the dolly’s independently powered acceleration, braking and steering, and sway controls essentially remove the need to own a truck in the first place.

The dolly system’s truck bed sides and small size allow users to experience the functionality and utility of a truck only when they need it, allowing them to own a smaller, cheaper, and more fuel efficient vehicle that suits daily use needs.

There are some pretty obvious practical questions still to answer, of course, including how much battery capacity the dolly would need, how much weight it could handle and how it would perform on long grades or in emergency braking situations. And, to be clear, a patent isn’t a product announcement or proof that Stellantis plans to put one of these things on sale – heck, if I were Stellantis’ CEO, I’d patent this thing just to prevent anyone else from building one so I could keep selling ancient, low-tech, high-margin Ram Trucks – but it’s a neat idea.

That is a funny picture with the tiny 500e "pulling" that huge trailer.

But on a more serious note, there's so much that goes into pulling. It's control. It's stopping. It's being smart enough to watch the weather forecast and know when to pull off the road and sit out a storm.

The irony here? Back in 2004, I began working at a dealership selling Chrysler, Dodge, Ram and Jeep. So of course we had the big trucks and many came in buying the 2500/3500 with the Cummins Diesel. Chrysler Corp made every sales person go through specialized training for the trucks and towing. Every sale had to include a form signed by the customer about towing and the limits of the truck they were buying. Hidden in there was a clause that stated the customer would NOT use the truck to tow more than the listed (legal) amount. If the customer didn't sign it, we were told by Chrysler that would be a no sale. They were very serious, and for good reason.

I may not like seeing all these huge trucks on the road. But when it comes to towing, mass is your friend. A powerful engine, huge (good) brakes and a well trained driver are a must.

I think it’s neat, anyway. What do you guys think? Are you ready to trade in your big-battery Chevy Silverado EV or Volvo VNR 800 on a new Topolino, or are you going to keep driving inefficient 99% of the time? Let us know, in the comments.

#4399. Tesla Drivers Can Now Plug In And Charge Automatically at Ionna Stations

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Tesla drivers can now seamlessly charge their electric cars at Ioona Rechargeries using a feature called Autocharge, as reported by State of Charge. With Autocharge, EVs can simply be plugged in, and the session will start automatically, without the driver having to do anything. Billing is also handled automatically, but a one-time setup needs to be completed to enable the functionality to work in the background.

In Tesla and Ionna’s case, a third-party smartphone application is needed to get started, as the charging network doesn’t have its own app. Drivers need to download and set up the Presto Charging app, which bundles over 190,000 chargers across the United States.

The setup involves creating an account with Presto Charging, scanning the car’s VIN for validation, and manually starting the first charging session in the app. While the initial charging session is active, an “Enable Autocharge” option will appear on the screen, which needs to be confirmed by the driver.

After this initial learning session, charging at Ionna locations will start automatically, and the driver’s payment method will be used to pay for the dispensed energy automatically.

To be clear, Presto Charging’s Autocharge function is not the same as Plug & Charge, even though it works in a similar way. With Plug & Charge, the EV communicates directly with the charger using a digital certificate, while Autocharge uses the car’s charging port network address to identify the vehicle and authorize it with a specific charger. In this case, the Presto Charging app takes the car’s information, checks it, and passes it to the charger, which starts the charging session.

Ionna Rechargeries feature CCS and NACS connectors

Plug & Charge is generally regarded as being a more secure option, but Presto Charging claims it constantly monitors sessions to prevent any issues. For instance, if the same vehicle appears as charging in a different location than the charger, the platform can flag it and fix it. Presto Charging handles all of the charging history and user data, which could be useful, considering Ionna doesn’t offer a way of keeping track of charging stops at its stations.

To make the feature more appealing to Tesla owners, the first session using Autocharge at Ionna is free. After that, pricing will be similar to Ionna’s regular offering, though it’s important to note that Presto Charging will get a small share to keep the lights on and squash any potential bugs. Other automakers have enabled Plug & Charge at Ionna, and drivers can use the card terminals at all stations to pay for charging.

It’s an important step for Ionna, which is still small compared to Tesla’s own Supercharger network, but has made significant progress when it comes to the quality of charging sessions. According to J.D. Power’s latest driver satisfaction survey, Ionna ranked first, and it’s hardly surprising, given how we’ve always had great experiences with the company’s chargers. They always work, they’re fast, and there are clean amenities nearby.

Last month, Ionna opened its 200th station, marking a huge milestone for the up-and-coming company. In total, the network now has over 1,600 ports across the country—double compared to seven months ago—and it’s not slowing down. No fewer than 80 new locations are under construction, and more are planned.

#4398. $20K Nissan NX7 PHEV goes on sale with nearly 200 miles of electric range

Dongfeng Nissan officially opened the early order book on its new NX7 hybrid yesterday, promising up to 320 km (~198 miles) of all-electric range from a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery and a $20,000 price tag.

When the first generation Nissan LEAF bowed with 70-ish miles of range from its 24 kWh li-ion battery pack, it struggled to meet widespread adoption, especially in an SUV-obsessed US market that demands forethought-free trips to Home Depot and bladder-busting range. The company’s latest 2027 Rogue Hybrid is a step in the right direction, using a gas engine to generate electricity for a pair of electric drive motors that deliver a driving experience that’s remarkably similar to a “pure” electric car – but without a plug, it’s still entirely dependent on fossil fuels. The new Dongfeng Nissan NX7, though? That’s a different story.

The plug-in hybrid Dongfeng Nissan NX7 might be called a “long range hybrid” in the same sense that Volvo’s Euro-market XC70 is, in that it’s an EV for the 360-odd days a year that you’re driving less than 200 miles, and an ICE vehicle for the handful of days you drive more. And if you’re one of those people who thinks stopping on road trips is a character flaw, a fully charged and topped off NX7 will take you an astonishing 1,666 km (~1,035 miles) from where you started.

The new NX7 could be an ideal lilypad vehicle for North American drivers who are either too afraid of being caught without a charger or too invested in the outcome of one or more dumb oil wars to confidently make the switch to EV – and, even at twice the 129,900 yuan ($~19,400) asking price, I think it would be a hit.

For that money, NX7 buyers get an absolutely loaded Model Y-sized crossover (they’re within 1/4″ of each other in length), with a 17.3″ central touchscreen, a fully digital instrument cluster, and (on higher-spec models) a positively massive 55″ augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P automotive processor and running on Nissan OS 3.0 with an AI-powered voice assistant developed with iFlytek that, Nissan claims, can recognize natural-language commands, remember user preferences, and even recognize occupants, adjusting vehicle settings accordingly.

On top-shelf models, the NX7 cabins get “AI Zero-Pressure Cloud Blanket” seats that use sensors and air-cushion arrays to dynamically adjust for maximum comfort, and include heating, ventilation, and a 12-point SPA-level massage function. The front seats can be fully reclined to create a bed-like configuration that will be familiar to Cube owners. The NX7 even offers an on-board refrigerator and motion-sickness prevention system that Nissan claims can reduce motion sickness by as much as 83% (which, like, I wouldn’t want to be the one to test that – but seems cool).

Power comes from a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated internal combustion engine making 98 hp that’s paired to a 228 hp electric drive motor and the previously mentioned 40.9 kWh LFP battery. It’s not immediately clear if the NX7 uses a conventional parallel hybrid system like a Prius or a series-hybrid-plus-plug setup, but Dongfeng’s hybrid technology patents describe a pretty versatile arrangement with four possible operating modes: series hybrid, parallel hybrid, direct engine drive and electricity generation – which means the vehicle can theoretically use the ICE motor as a generator, drive the wheels mechanically, or work alongside the electric motor, depending on what the operating conditions call for. Whether any or all four modes make it to production on the NX7 remains to be seen, but it’s an intriguing bit of engineering for a vehicle promising nearly 200 miles of electric driving range.

Electrek is really going downhill fast. Not only is the app extremely glitchy where you have to repeatedly close videos that don’t play and prevent you from reading the articles, they then leave out important information in those articles such as “this vehicle will not be available in the United States.”

The final production version will be shown to the public for the first time at the Guangzhou Auto Show later this month, but you can let us know what you think of the new NX7 in the comments, today.

#4396. China’s electric airliner era starts with a 19-seat plane and 400 km of range

COMAC’s CE-25A, China’s 19-seat battery-electric commuter plane, flew with a crew for the first time on Saturday in Binzhou, Shandong. Two pilots and a flight test engineer were aboard the roughly 10-tonne demonstrator, and COMAC says every system worked normally.

It wasn’t the plane’s first flight. The CE-25A had already completed 19 autonomous test flights with nobody on board since February 2, and China’s aviation regulator is now reviewing it for a type certificate.

The CE-25A is a T-tail commuter plane with 10 electric ducted fans on the wings, five per side, instead of propellers. COMAC lists a 300 km/h cruise speed and a 400 km (250-mile) range.

The CAAC accepting COMAC’s type certificate application starts the airworthiness review. It doesn’t mean paying passengers are close, and COMAC hasn’t given a date for commercial service.

The program has been quiet for a long time. COMAC showed a CE-25A model at the China International Import Expo in Shanghai in November 2023, with a placard listing 400 to 500 km of range and a 400 km/h top cruise speed. The full-size aircraft, registered B-0EFH, only became public when photos leaked on Chinese social media on October 28.

The obvious battery candidate is CATL. In July 2023, COMAC, CATL, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University formed a joint venture with CNY 600 million in registered capital to develop electric aircraft, as we reported when CATL launched its aviation unit.

CATL had just unveiled its “condensed” battery at the time, claiming up to 500 Wh/kg at the cell level, and said it was testing the cells to aviation standards. Neither company has confirmed what’s inside the CE-25A, though.

~500 Wh/kg has long been seen as the target for battery energy density to enable electric flight on a commercial scale.

COMAC isn’t alone in flying a large electric demonstrator. In August, Heart Aerospace flew its X1 in Plattsburgh, New York, for 27 minutes. It’s a 25,000-lb aircraft with a 106-foot wingspan, which Heart calls the largest battery-electric aircraft ever flown.

Eviation flew its 9-passenger Alice back in September 2022, then laid off most of its staff in early 2025.

Heart is the closest Western comparison. It dropped its 19-seat ES-19 for the 30-seat ES-30 back in 2022, and the ES-30 now relies on reserve turbogenerators to stretch its range, with BAE Systems working on the battery. Heart is targeting 2031 for service and claims “more than 40%” lower operating costs.

For years, the go-to excuse in the West for doing nothing about emissions was China. Why should we bother, the argument went, if China won’t? Now China is pulling ahead, and it’s doing it by cutting its dependence on fossil fuels.

Look at trucking. Electric trucks hit 50.3% of China’s heavy truck sales in September, and they’re already eating into the country’s diesel demand. In the US, electric models were about 0.3% of heavy-truck sales last year, according to the ICCT.

A great step in the right direction, probably needs a doubling in range but at current rates of progress that will only be five years away.

Now it’s planes, starting where batteries make sense today: short regional routes. The CE-25A’s 400 km shrinks once you keep the reserves regulators require, and a Beechcraft 1900 turboprop in the same class covers well over 1,000 km. So it’s not replacing turboprops anytime soon. But that’s how trucking started too. Short-haul first, then long-haul tractors once the batteries caught up.

And this couldn’t happen fast enough. We’re in the middle of a diesel and jet fuel crisis. Jet fuel averaged $3.50 a gallon in early August, up 63% from a year earlier, according to Heart Aerospace. Every truck and plane China moves to batteries is one less exposed to that.

China also has the batteries to pull it off, with CATL in the joint venture. Meanwhile, Heart has pushed to 2031 and added a fuel-burning backup, and Eviation is a cautionary tale.

#4395. Tesla Just Bumped The Cheapest Model Y’s Range, But The Price Stays The Same

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Tesla has increased the estimated range for its most affordable Model Y trim. The 2027 Tesla Model Y Rear-Wheel Drive is now listed on the American company’s website as being capable of driving up to 348 miles on a full charge, up from 321 miles before.

With the standard 18-inch wheels, the crossover gets an 8% bump in range, but with the optional 19-inch wheels, the base-spec Model Y can now cover up to 335 miles, a 10% increase.

It’s unclear what Tesla did to improve the range of the most affordable Model Y, but one thing is certain: the price. Just like before, the entry-level crossover starts at $41,630. The range change is not yet reflected on the EPA’s website, which still lists the old 321-mile rating, but that will likely change in the future, as the company submits new paperwork.

The longer range brings the most affordable Model Y just seven miles shy of the more expensive Premium trim’s estimated driving distance. The Model Y Premium costs $6,000 more and offers faster acceleration, slightly more range, a revised exterior design, and a more upmarket interior.

Features like an FM radio, heated rear seats, a rear passenger display, adaptive high beams, and frequency-dependent shock absorbers can only be had on the Premium or higher trims. The entry-level Model Y also comes with a glass roof that’s covered by a one-piece headliner.

This is just the latest reshuffle of Tesla’s lineup. Last week, the most affordable all-wheel-drive Model Y disappeared from the company’s U.S. portfolio, and earlier this month, Tesla decided that the Cybertruck would go out of production in 2027. The Model S and Model X were axed, too.

At the same time, however, Tesla claims that it’s ramping up production of the Cybercab two-seater and its Optimus humanoid robot. The company has also boosted production of the Semi electric truck and is now taking reservations for the outrageous Roadster, which made headlines after doing a backflip and jumping over several cars.

Until that happens, though, Tesla has started inviting “select customers” to order Cybercabs, but the cars won’t be able to operate anywhere in the country. According to the terms, the vehicles will only work in “supported service areas” and only if the owner pays a $299 monthly subscription for autonomous driving.

#4394. Tested: The 2026 Lexus ES Hybrid Evolves, but It Has a Familiar Feel

Larger than before and with a significantly revamped interior, the new ES350h nonetheless stays the course with its cushy driving demeanor.

11/12/26 UPDATE: This review has been updated with instrumented test results.

Although Lexus is no stranger to sporty models, this luxury brand made its name on quiet, plush sedans that prioritize refinement above all else. And the ES is the one that has persisted. This comfy cruiser was the bestselling Lexus for many years, and it continues to attract a loyal set of buyers. Understandably, Lexus has been reluctant to change the ES formula much throughout its seven generations thus far.

On the surface, that appears to change with the new eighth-generation Lexus ES. Not only does the ES look quite different inside and out for 2026, but it also offers an electric powertrain for the first time. The ES hybrid continues, however, and after driving the latest version, it’s clear that this sedan's core mission hasn't changed as much as you might think.

Lexus first offered the ES as a hybrid for 2013, and the previous-generation gas-electric model made up around 40 percent of ES sales last year. Given that take rate, it makes sense that the old nonhybrid V-6 has been axed. The electric ES, which we review separately, is a big departure for this model line, but Lexus expects the hybrid to make up 80 percent of ES sales in the U.S. So, for now at least, the EV will be a niche product, and the gas-electric model will be the volume seller.

See all results for new 2026 Lexus ES for sale near 60007

With a longer wheelbase, a significantly taller profile, and a more imposing shape, the new ES stretches to the larger end of the mid-size luxury-sedan segment. Lexus engineers say they tried to “eliminate the negatives” of the sedan shape with this model, such as the more difficult ingress and egress of a lower seating height. In other words, it follows the tall-sedan format of the Toyota Crown but attempts to disguise its stature with more angular styling and a swoopy roofline that tapers toward the short trunk lid. There are some awkward angles, but overall, the design works and is still recognizable as a Lexus.

The ES hybrid gets the latest Toyota hybrid powertrain, which the company refers to as the sixth-generation setup. It has a different power unit and transmission than before, and it’s configured to prioritize the electric motors for propulsion more. The 2.5-liter gasoline four-cylinder engine doesn’t change much, but total combined output of 244 horsepower is up from the previous ES300h’s 215 horses. That’s apparently enough for Lexus to bump the badge up to ES350h. All-wheel drive is optional on the hybrid ES for the first time, courtesy of an additional electric motor on the rear axle, though it doesn’t change output figures compared with the front-wheel-drive configuration.

The all-wheel-drive ES350h we tested got to 60 mph in 6.6 seconds, which is a significant improvement over the previous, front-wheel-drive ES300h F Sport’s 7.9-second run. That’s despite a significant weight gain, as our test car tipped the scales at 4145 pounds, 352 more than the 2023 ES300h we last tested.

See all results for new 2026 Lexus ES for sale near 60007

While this four-cylinder powertrain isn’t quite as smooth or sonorous as the old nonhybrid ES350’s V-6, the upgraded gas-electric setup is appreciably more refined than the old hybrid was. The gas engine is well isolated from the cabin and only makes itself known under hard acceleration; the hushed 67 decibels and 21 sones of noise we recorded inside at 70 mph is perfectly acceptable here. The electric motors go about their business seamlessly, with imperceptible switching between gas and electric power, and while the embiggened ES doesn’t quite feel eager, it accelerates with sufficient gusto and generally is responsive to throttle inputs. EPA ratings sit at 46 mpg combined with front-wheel drive and 44 mpg with all-wheel drive—strong numbers for this large of a sedan. We averaged 37 mpg overall, and the ES matched its 42-mpg EPA highway estimate in our 75-mph real-world fuel-economy test. But that’s not quite as good as the previous model, a 2019 ES300h which managed 45 mpg in the same test.

Importantly, the ride quality is fantastic. The suspension is tuned to be soft, as you’d expect for a boulevardier like this, but we appreciate the nicely controlled body motions. And the all-season tires have plenty of sidewall for soaking up potholes and rough sections of road (relatively small 19-inch wheels are the only choice on the hybrid model for now). This isn’t a vehicle for hard cornering, and the eco-conscious rubber doesn’t provide much grip when you push it around corners, but the steering wheel feels good in your hands and provides satisfactory on-center feel and natural effort buildup. We recorded a ho-hum 0.84 g of grip around our skidpad and a 170-foot stop from 70 mph.

Upon first glance at the cabin, you might worry that Lexus has too eagerly adopted the button-free, touch-capacitive interiors that are becoming too commonplace. And while there are definitely fewer buttons and knobs than before, and more controls integrated into the large 14.0-inch touchscreen, Lexus has done a good job balancing function with form. There’s still a volume knob, for instance, and although most climate functions are now on a lower part of the screen, there are a few crucial tactile buttons for adjusting the temperature and turning on the defrosters. The steering-wheel controls look like they’re touch-sensitive, but they’re thankfully tactile too. And the secondary functions such as mirror controls, seat adjustments, and windows are all still conventional and intuitive.

The material finishes and build quality live up to Lexus’s high standard. But it is worth noting that the hybrid comes in Premium and Premium+ trims, which means it doesn’t offer some of the most high-end features and accoutrements of the electric model’s Luxury trim. Pricing for the ES350h ($51,095 to start) is up $6380 over the previous ES300h, but you do get more car—namely in the physical sense—and the ES still costs significantly less than a BMW 5-series or a Mercedes-Benz E-class. Our Premium-trim test car featured a few options and still came in at under $55,000.

Lexus is notoriously risk-averse with its most popular models, and ultimately the company’s conservatism has paid off with this new ES. It’s more modern-looking inside and out and offers more technology than before, but Lexus wisely didn’t make many changes to the core tenets that have made the ES a success. It still offers a comfortable ride and a cosseting interior, and these qualities combined with the hybrid powertrain’s quiet operation and impressive fuel efficiency should continue to please the ES faithful.

#4393. High altitude, bitter cold, zero drivers: autonomous trucks take on Tibetan mine

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

Chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

“High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”

That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the company won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors, adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the big bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

“Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is currently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines, including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

While specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the company has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain, pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.

Those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The big trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

#4392. Scout’s New Truck and SUV Are Another Step Closer to Reality

The VW-owned company has started validation builds of the Terra and Traveler at its new $2 billion factory in Blythewood, South Carolina.

Just like vehicles themselves, automotive manufacturing plants have to go through a lot of testing before cranking out the first production model. Scout Motors broke ground on its Blythewood, South Carolina, plant about two and a half years ago, and as final bits of construction wrap up, the VW Group subsidiary is beginning to build validation vehicles to test production processes.

When Scout reemerged a few years ago to bring back the practical, can-do vehicles that defined the brand in the 1960s and ’70s, it aimed to build a fleet of hybrid and electric body-on-frame off-roaders that blended modern amenities with vintage charm. The automaker plans to launch a Terra pickup truck and a Traveler SUV for the 2028 model year.

See all results for new 2028 Scout Terra for sale near 94043

It looks like Scout is still on track to stick with that timeline. The automaker has announced that most of the manufacturing parts are already up and running, with validation vehicles beginning to make their way through the body, paint, and assembly shops. Validation vehicles are kind of like a practice run, giving employees the ability to problem-solve and refine processes without having to keep a tight schedule.

Alongside the new equipment, Scout is testing out more than 750 robots in the body shop. The AI-supported bots will be used to monitor about 5000 weld points per vehicle for quality assurance. At full capacity, the body shop will be able to process about 40 vehicles per hour.

The Terra pickup and Traveler SUV are both expected to start at under $60,000. Scout says the validation process will continue into 2027, followed by more refined pre-production vehicles and eventually the finalized production model. That’s right in line with what Scott Keogh, Scout’s CEO, told us last year, when he projected that the first vehicles would go on sale by the end of 2027. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2028.

#4391. Mowing milestone: Greenzie surpasses 255,000 autonomous miles mowed

Autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie announced the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet, the company really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

“We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” says Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”

Greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial, as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

“Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” said Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of big battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

The company says the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.

A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.

Let’s get some pro-labor rage going in the comments, and don’t forget to mention what kind of paycheck you’d need to get to go work in landscaping 2,000+ hours a year while you’re there.

It's time for us to accept that there are more jobs that don't make sense for humans. We are already ok with machines doing all kinds of things that used to be human. When people get spooked and want to hold the line outright, it's wasted effort. Flailing and fussing is counterproductive. We need to be focusing on where we actually need to keep humans. We need to be thoughtful and deliberate about human labor and workers' rights and start planning (belatedly) for a smooth (if we're smart and lucky) transition to a radically restructured economy. The alternative will make the great depression pale in comparison.

#4390. BMW’s iX5 Beat The Lucid Gravity On Highway Range. Not On Efficiency

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BMW’s answer to electric SUV range anxiety involves a battery big enough to make some other EVs look underfed. The new iX5 packs 144 kilowatt-hours of usable capacity, which gives it an EPA range of 435 miles. But EVs can’t typically match their official range claim when driven at a constant 70 mph on the highway.

The iX5 came very close to matching it in this Out Of Spec Testing group range test, though. It covered 410.8 miles, putting it ahead of the Lucid Gravity Grand Touring, Rivian R1S Dual Max, and Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric. It wasn’t the most frugal SUV here; it simply combined respectable efficiency with an enormous energy reserve.

There’s an asterisk next to that headline range number, though. The BMW initially shut down at around 400 miles (644 km). However, they were able to get it moving again, which unlocked enough remaining energy to keep going at highway speed and extend the range.

Video host Kyle Conner notes that the BMW initially shut down after going through almost exactly 144 kWh, its stated usable battery capacity. At that point, it had been showing 0% remaining in the battery for around 10 miles.

Restarting it added another 4 kWh, allowing it to continue at 70 mph (113 km/h). Kyle speculated that the car might deliberately stop after delivering its rated capacity, leaving some remaining energy accessible after a restart, but stressed that this was a theory rather than a confirmed explanation from BMW.

The Lucid Gravity Grand Touring finished second, covering 367.7 miles (592 km) at 70 mph (113 km/h) with its 123-kWh battery. The Rivian R1S Dual Max followed at 349 miles (562 km), although the testers extracted only around 136 kWh from its aging pack (it had nearly 30,000 miles on its odometer), versus roughly 145 kWh in an earlier test. The Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric finished last at 309 miles (497 km).

We’ve seen the Gravity miss its EPA figure on the highway before. In a previous test, it recorded 345 miles, although Lucid flagged a possible rear drive-unit problem with that vehicle, which may have affected the result. Different conditions and test endpoints also mean those results aren’t directly comparable.

Porsche, meanwhile, puts more emphasis on how its SUV drives than outright efficiency. The Cayenne Turbo Electric brought a performance-focused powertrain, 21-inch aero wheels, and a towing package, yet it still used less energy per mile than the BMW. Its limiting factor was the smallest battery here at 108 kWh, despite showing higher efficiency than both the BMW and Rivian; it finished roughly 102 miles behind the winner.

The iX5’s win here is convincing, even considering the restart. The Gravity squeezed more miles out of each kilowatt-hour, but the BMW simply had more of them to spend. Sometimes the answer to range anxiety really seems to be just a bigger battery.

#4389. Is Tesla rushing out a half-baked Cybercab just to shave MKBHD’s head?

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

Surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

After Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) said there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a new video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”

On Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

As we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement says it “will not operate” without the $299 plan, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

So Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

Brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

The memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:

“It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”

That’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

Yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

Tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version shows up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself says is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

This Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

What do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.

You can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.

This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.

#4388. 2027 McLaren W1

See all results for new 2027 McLaren W1 for sale near 07011

They say that lightning never strikes the same place twice, let alone thrice, but McLaren is channeling Zeus with its newest W1 flagship. As a descendant of the hallowed McLaren F1 and a direct successor to the brand's last 903-hp P1 halo car, the W1 assumes a throne previously occupied by hypercar royalty. And if you couldn’t guess by its wind-sculpted, carbon-fiber-laden exterior, the W1 has the spec sheet to back up its noble position.

Wielding a 9200-rpm twin-turbo V-8 paired with an axial-flux electric motor, the W1 delivers 1258 horsepower to the pavement via its rear wheels, making it the most powerful McLaren ever. Those ponies don’t have to contend with much mass, as a carbon-fiber tub and body help keep the W1's dry weight to a feathery 3084 pounds. Active aerodynamics, including a rear wing that extends rearward up to 11.8 inches, add massive downforce and enable maximum attack at the racetrack. The W1 is a worthy heir to its predecessors, the latest in a highly accomplished bloodline of supersonic, roadgoing weaponry.

Expert Tip: When it comes to seven-digit, Formula-1-inspired race cars for the road, options are predictably limited. The Aston Martin Valhalla is another example, brandishing a 1064-horsepower plug-in-hybrid powertrain and a chassis developed with help from the Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team.

With the W1 debuting just last year, we don’t expect any changes for the 2027 model year.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The W1 uses a plug-in hybrid powertrain comprised of McLaren's MHP-8 turbocharged V-8 engine working in unison with a radial-flux electric motor and an 8-speed transmission; it sends power to the rear wheels. The V-8 alone is good for 916 horsepower, and the electric motor 342 horsepower. Combined, that's 1258 ponies, the highest output of any McLaren.

The electric element includes a motorsport-derived E-module: a radial flux motor and integrated Motor Control Unit weighing just 44 pounds, similar to the type used in IndyCar racing. (McLaren participates in that series as well as F1.) The electric motor is mounted to the transmission and can spin up to 24,000 rpm. The E-module is powered by a battery of about 1.4 kWh, enclosed in a structural carbon-fiber box located low in the chassis to optimize the center of gravity. The battery maintains a minimum level of charge to crank the engine on vehicle start-up and to power the electric reversing function. McLaren quotes an electric-only driving range of about two miles and a charging time of 22 minutes to bring the battery to 80 percent.

According to McLaren, the W1 can hit 60 mph in just 2.7 seconds. More remarkably, accelerating from 0-124 mph requires just 5.8 seconds. #4387. BMW Just Started Making EV Batteries In America. The New iX5 Will Be First In Line

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

BMW’s first high-voltage battery factory for electric vehicles in the United States is now up and running in Woodruff, South Carolina. The facility, which is located just 15 miles from the automaker’s car factory in Spartanburg, will supply finished battery packs for no fewer than six Neue Klasse EVs assembled in the U.S., starting with the new iX5 SUV.

According to BMW, the new facility doesn’t build cells from scratch. Instead, it sources ready-made cells from local suppliers, which are then checked at the plant under a “zero-defect” policy. BMW says it will source Gen6 cylindrical cells from LG Energy Solution in the U.S., while Samsung SDI will supply European factories.

BMW EV battery factory in Woodruff, South Carolina

After analyzing each incoming cell for voltage and other parameters, the factory starts the clustering process, where the battery cells are connected to coolers to ensure optimal insulation and cooling. While the packs go down the assembly line, they are continuously monitored in real time to make sure that each pack goes out the door in tip-top condition.

The company’s latest EV batteries are built using the “cell-to-pack” technique, where cells are no longer arranged in modules. Instead, they’re put directly into the pack enclosure, where they’re protected by a hardened foam. This way, more cells can fit into the same volume, leading to more energy density and more driving range.

In South Carolina, all production staff go through a virtual reality training program, so they can practice real manufacturing operations under realistic conditions before they set foot on the assembly line. What’s more, BMW is relying heavily on artificial intelligence-powered digital assistants and more than 250 robots to output zero-defect batteries. Over 300 employees are currently working at the company’s new battery-making facility.

The Woodruff plant is BMW’s fourth site in its Gen6 battery production network to start series production, after the facilities in Debrecen, Hungary, Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Germany, Shenyang, China, and San Luis Potosí, Mexico.

It took the automaker roughly three years to go from groundbreaking to mass production in South Carolina. Construction of the Woodruff plant began in September 2023, and just one year later, in September 2024, the first manufacturing equipment was installed. In summer 2025, the first pre-series batteries rolled off the assembly line.

What makes the new facility special, besides being BMW’s first battery plant in the U.S., is that during normal operation, it doesn’t use any fossil fuels, with the site’s industrial trucks being powered by hydrogen. As for the latest Gen6 cylindrical cells, they’re touted as having 28% fewer carbon dioxide emissions compared to the cells used in the outgoing iX SUV.

When the rear seats are folded, the electric ID. Cross offers up to 1,345 liters of overall luggage volume.

#4384. Even occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke

New preliminary research involving more than 440,000 American adults has uncovered a concerning association between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease, particularly stroke. The findings suggest that even occasional marijuana use may be linked to higher odds of cardiovascular problems, raising new questions about the health effects of a substance that is becoming increasingly common across the United States.

The research, presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, found that the association was not limited to people who frequently used cannabis. It also appeared across different methods of consumption (smoked or edible, etc.). Researchers emphasized that cannabis use should be considered when discussing heart health and stroke prevention.

Scientific Sessions 2026 took place November 6 through 9 in Chicago, bringing together cardiovascular researchers and healthcare professionals from around the world to share scientific discoveries, clinical advances, and emerging evidence.

Cannabis refers to the plant itself, while marijuana is a commonly used term for cannabis products containing enough THC to produce psychoactive effects.

Marijuana Use Is Rising Across the United States

"Previous research has indicated that cannabis use is rapidly increasing in the United States, with 1 in 6 adults in 2024 reporting having used it within the last month, up from 1 in 10 in 2020 -- a 51% increase," said study author Aabha Divya, M.B.B.S., M.Ch., an assistant professor in the division of cardiothoracic surgery at the Tulane University School of Medicine in New Orleans.

Earlier research conducted between 2016 and 2020 had already identified associations between cannabis consumption and unfavorable cardiovascular outcomes. Those findings also suggested that using cannabis more frequently during a given month was connected to greater cardiovascular risk.

However, the evidence has not always been consistent. With recreational marijuana becoming legal in more places and cannabis products increasingly available, Divya and colleagues wanted to investigate these possible health effects in a larger population.

"We wanted to expand on this earlier work because cannabis use has become increasingly common in the United States, as recreational legalization and commercial availability of various products with cannabis have also expanded. Previous studies have raised concerns about possible cardiovascular effects; however, the results have not been consistent," Divya said.

The researchers examined information collected through the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), a large telephone survey of American adults. They combined responses from jurisdictions that collected information about cannabis consumption between 2020 and 2024.

Participants answered questions about their marijuana use and whether a healthcare professional had ever diagnosed them with cardiovascular conditions, including a heart attack, stroke, or coronary heart disease.

Even Occasional Marijuana Use Was Linked to Higher Stroke Odds

One of the most striking findings was that infrequent cannabis use was associated with cardiovascular problems. In fact, the researchers did not find the steady increase in cardiovascular risk with more frequent use that they had expected.

The analysis revealed several important associations:

These findings were unexpected because the relationship between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease did not consistently become stronger as consumption increased.

"We were surprised to find that the link between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease was not straightforward. We expected that the chances of heart disease would gradually rise as people used cannabis more often, but that wasn't the case. Both low-use and heavy-use groups had higher odds of developing heart disease," Divya said.

Although the study cannot establish that marijuana directly causes strokes or other cardiovascular conditions, the findings suggest that occasional consumption should not automatically be considered free of potential cardiovascular concerns.

"As cannabis use becomes more common, it is increasingly important that people and their healthcare professionals include it in conversations about cardiovascular health, just as they discuss tobacco, alcohol and other commonly used substances," she added.

Experts Urge Greater Attention to Cannabis and Heart Health

Robert L. Page II, Pharm.D., M.S.P.H., FAHA, who led the writing group responsible for the American Heart Association's 2020 cannabis scientific statement, said the findings add to growing concerns about marijuana's possible cardiovascular effects.

One challenge in evaluating those effects is that many cannabis users also smoke tobacco. Because tobacco is already an established cardiovascular risk factor, separating its effects from those of cannabis can be difficult.

Page, who was not involved in the research, explained why the new findings deserve attention.

"Unfortunately, many patients who use cannabis may also smoke tobacco, which completely clouds the issue when addressing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. In patients who use both, cannabis has always been considered an innocent bystander; however, this is not the case. This is the second observational study to suggest that cannabis exposure (without tobacco smoking) may be a potential risk factor for developing cardiovascular disease. Overall, cannabis is beginning to emerge as a major contributor to premature heart disease in young and older adults, which can lead to serious cardiovascular events. To this end, clinicians should be addressing cannabis use with their patients as they would tobacco use when considering the risk of cardiovascular disease."

Page is a professor in the department of clinical pharmacy and the department of physical medicine/rehabilitation at the University of Colorado Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences in Aurora, Colorado.

How Researchers Studied Nearly Half a Million Americans

The analysis included 442,906 adults living in the United States (average age of 49 years; approximately half women). Their responses came from telephone surveys conducted through the BRFSS.

Researchers used survey information collected from 2020 through 2024, focusing on states that had included an optional marijuana questionnaire. Between 16 and 24 states participated in this portion of the survey each year, meaning the analysis did not represent every state.

Participants reported how many days they had consumed cannabis during the preceding month. The questions covered multiple ways of using marijuana (smoking, vaping or ingesting gummies or other cannabis-containing foods).

The researchers divided participants into four categories based on their reported use:

Participants also indicated whether they had ever received a diagnosis of heart attack, heart disease, heart-related chest pain, or stroke.

To better distinguish the association with cannabis from other potential explanations, the researchers accounted for numerous established cardiovascular risk factors. These included demographic characteristics, tobacco smoking, alcohol consumption, obesity, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, physical inactivity, education, and income.

Why the Findings Do Not Prove Marijuana Causes Strokes

Despite the large number of participants, the study has several limitations that affect how its findings should be interpreted.

First, the analysis examined associations between reported cannabis use and previously diagnosed cardiovascular conditions at a single point in time. This means researchers could not determine whether marijuana use preceded the cardiovascular problems or whether it directly contributed to them.

The information also depended on participants accurately recalling and reporting their cannabis consumption and medical histories (making them subject to potential errors in memory). Such reports may not always reflect actual patterns of use or diagnoses.

Another limitation was the lack of information about the strength of the cannabis products participants consumed or the quantities they used. Without those details, the researchers could not evaluate whether THC potency or the amount consumed influenced the observed associations.

The researchers also acknowledged that some participants may have reduced or discontinued cannabis consumption after being diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. As a result, the group reporting no cannabis use in the previous month may have included former users.

These uncertainties make it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how consumption frequency affects cardiovascular health. Nevertheless, the findings add to growing evidence that cannabis use deserves closer examination as a possible factor in heart disease and stroke.

As marijuana becomes more widely available and its use continues to increase, researchers and healthcare professionals are emphasizing the importance of discussing cannabis alongside other substances that may affect cardiovascular health.

#4383. Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest

Energy drinks and stimulant supplements are raising new concerns about heart health after researchers discovered a striking pattern in reports of serious cardiovascular emergencies. Products containing caffeine and other stimulants appeared far more frequently in reports of cardiac arrest, heart attacks, and other heart problems than products without these ingredients.

The findings were particularly concerning among younger adults. People ages 18 to 34 accounted for a substantial share of the reported heart problems involving caffeinated products, according to independent, preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026.

Researchers emphasized that the findings do not establish that energy drinks or stimulant supplements caused these medical emergencies. However, the unusually high frequency of certain cardiovascular events in FDA safety reports suggests that these widely available products deserve closer examination.

Growing Concerns About Energy Drinks and Heart Health

The energy drink industry has expanded rapidly, with sales more than doubling over the past decade and exceeding $20 billion in 2024. Despite their popularity, scientists still have limited information about the cardiovascular effects of energy drinks and supplements containing stimulants.

Existing evidence suggests that consuming large amounts of caffeine can harm the cardiovascular system. Medical professionals have also documented cases of arrhythmias (irregular heart rhythms) and sudden cardiac death following the consumption of these products. Some of these incidents involved young adults who had no previously identified risk factors for heart disease.

A 2026 American Heart Association Scientific Statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease indicates that most adults can generally consume up to 400 mg of caffeine daily without significant safety concerns (the equivalent of up to 5, 8-ounce cups of regular black caffeinated coffee).

However, caffeine concentrations can differ dramatically between products. Certain energy drinks provide up to three times as much caffeine per fluid ounce as brewed coffee, while some pre-workout supplements contain more than 12 times the concentration found in coffee.

Another concern involves how these products are regulated. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) classifies energy drinks and stimulant supplements as foods or dietary supplements rather than medications. As a result, they are not subject to the same safety testing requirements that medications must meet before entering the market.

"These products are marketed as everyday pick-me-ups and sold next to soda and bottled water, so most people assume they carry no real risk," said study author Sai Samayamanthula, a fourth-year medical student at the University of Virginia School of Medicine in Charlottesville, Virginia. "For many healthy people, if these products are consumed occasionally, the risk is probably small. However, individuals who consume energy drinks or other stimulant-containing supplements regularly can quickly exceed the recommended daily limit for caffeine, so it's important for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products."

FDA Reports Reveal Striking Differences in Cardiac Events

To investigate possible cardiovascular safety concerns, researchers examined a federal database containing reports of suspected adverse reactions to foods and dietary supplements. They compared products containing caffeine and other stimulants with products that did not contain these ingredients.

The comparison group included commonly consumed products such as soft drinks, smoothies, vitamins, protein bars, and meal replacement shakes. Researchers examined reports involving people ages 13 and older submitted between 2017 and 2025.

Several differences stood out in the analysis:

These differences describe how frequently certain medical problems appeared within the FDA reports. They do not mean that people consuming energy drinks face an 11 times greater actual risk of cardiac arrest or a 4.5 times greater risk of having a heart attack.

"Our findings support the case for more systematic safety monitoring of caffeine- and stimulant-containing products. In addition, healthcare professionals should remember to ask their younger patients who have palpitations, chest pain, or fainting spells if they recently or regularly consume these products," Samayamanthula said.

Why Young Adults May Be Particularly Vulnerable

One of the most notable findings was the large proportion of cardiovascular reports involving younger adults. Researchers have not yet determined why the connection between stimulant products and reported heart problems appeared so frequently in this age group.

Several explanations are possible. Younger consumers may use energy drinks and stimulant supplements more often, increasing the likelihood that these products appear in reports of medical emergencies.

How the products are consumed could also influence the pattern. Potential contributing factors include the circumstances surrounding their use (for example, consuming them before intense exercise or mixing them with alcohol or drugs). Some individuals may also have previously undiagnosed heart conditions that could make them more susceptible to cardiovascular complications.

These possibilities remain uncertain, and additional research will be needed to determine which factors, if any, help explain the unusually high reporting frequency among younger adults.

Do Energy Drinks Actually Cause Heart Attacks?

Although the results raise important questions about products containing concentrated caffeine and other stimulants, experts caution against interpreting the findings as proof of a direct cause.

"This study raises concerns that products with very high amounts of caffeine may be harmful to the cardiovascular system," said Gregory M. Marcus, M.D., M.A.S., FAHA, chair of the 2026 American Heart Association scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease. "Although there are biological reasons why that connection could be possible, the study does not prove that caffeine products cause these events, because other factors may have influenced the results found in this analysis. More research is needed to understand whether these stimulant products are truly responsible for the reported heart-related events."

Marcus did not participate in the research. He is a professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine and serves as associate chief of the Cardiology for Research program at the University of California, San Francisco Health.

Because the analysis relied on reports submitted voluntarily to the FDA, it cannot establish whether the products themselves were responsible for the cardiovascular events. Other health conditions, behaviors, or circumstances may have played a role.

How Researchers Analyzed the FDA Safety Reports

The research team reviewed 28,345 reports of possible adverse events submitted to an FDA safety database from 2017 through 2025.

Of these, 854 reports involved energy drinks or dietary supplements containing caffeine or other stimulants. The remaining 27,491 reports concerned products without caffeine or stimulant ingredients and served as the comparison group.

Researchers classified products according to the ingredients they contained. The stimulant category included caffeine, methylxanthines (theobromine, guarana, yerba mate, green tea/coffee extracts) and sympathomimetics (synephrine, yohimbine, ephedra, DMAA, higenamine).

Rather than evaluating individual brands, the researchers grouped products by their ingredients. Consequently, the findings apply to broad categories of caffeinated and stimulant products and do not identify any particular brand as more dangerous than another.

The researchers also highlighted important limitations in the available data. Reports were voluntarily submitted by members of the public, consumers, healthcare professionals, and manufacturers, meaning that the database does not provide a complete record of everyone who experienced a possible adverse reaction.

Just as importantly, the researchers could not determine how many people consumed these products without developing cardiovascular problems. They also could not establish how many people experienced heart problems but never submitted a report.

Without those figures, the analysis cannot calculate the actual likelihood of a heart attack, cardiac arrest, or another cardiovascular event among consumers of energy drinks and stimulant supplements.

Nevertheless, the findings reveal a potentially important safety signal. Researchers say more systematic monitoring and further studies are needed to determine whether these products contribute directly to serious heart problems, particularly among younger adults who frequently consume them.

#4382. Walking and weight training may not be enough to keep your bones strong

The type of exercise you do may be more important for your bones than how long you spend doing it. Researchers at Semmelweis University have found that intense physical activity involving sudden bursts of movement, quick changes in direction, and sharp turns appears especially effective at stimulating new bone formation.

The findings, published in Sports Medicine - Open, suggest that certain fast-paced sports may provide greater benefits for bone metabolism than walking or conventional strength training. The research could help scientists develop more effective exercise recommendations for preserving bone health and reducing the risk of osteoporosis.

Why Exercise Intensity Matters for Bone Health

To investigate how different forms of exercise affect bones, the Semmelweis University team reviewed 24 clinical studies involving 1,238 healthy adults.

Instead of relying on bone mineral density measurements, which can take considerable time to reveal changes, the researchers examined blood markers associated with the production of new bone tissue. These biological indicators can reveal how bones respond to exercise within a matter of weeks, allowing scientists to detect changes much sooner.

"What makes our study unique is that we examined not only the type of exercise - whether endurance, resistance, or combined training - but also exercise intensity, frequency, and duration. Our goal was to determine which forms of exercise stimulate bone metabolism most effectively and which appear to be less beneficial from this perspective," said Dr. Péter Ferdinandy, Vice-Rector for Science and Innovations at Semmelweis University and senior author of the study.

Football and Handball Show Surprising Bone Benefits

The strongest responses were associated with vigorous sports that repeatedly require players to accelerate, change direction, turn, and make powerful movements.

Recreational football and handball stood out in particular. These activities were linked to increases of up to 45-46 percent in blood markers associated with bone formation, suggesting that they may provide a particularly strong stimulus for the body's bone-building processes.

More conventional activities generally produced smaller responses. Walking, step aerobics, and standard resistance workouts performed in the gym were less effective at stimulating the measured indicators of bone formation.

The findings were especially unexpected for resistance training, which is commonly recommended as a way to support skeletal health.

"The most surprising finding was that resistance training did not produce a significant effect on markers of bone metabolism, even though several professional guidelines recommend this type of exercise for maintaining bone health. Likewise, low- or moderate-intensity endurance exercise, such as walking or jogging, showed no meaningful long-term effect," explained Viktória Barna, PhD student at Semmelweis University and first author of the study.

Why Walking and Weight Training Still Matter

The results do not suggest that walking, jogging, or other less demanding activities should be abandoned. These forms of exercise continue to offer important health benefits, even if they do not stimulate the measured bone-building processes as strongly as more intense sports.

Rather, the research indicates that maintaining healthy bones may require greater mechanical stimulation than many everyday activities provide. Movements that place more substantial forces on the skeleton appear to produce a stronger response in the biological processes involved in forming new bone.

However, the researchers stress that people should not suddenly begin strenuous exercise without preparing appropriately.

This is especially important for individuals with cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, or metabolic conditions, as well as those who already have osteoporosis. Anyone in these groups who is considering a new activity or a more physically demanding exercise routine should first speak with their treating physician, general practitioner, or a sports medicine specialist. Medical guidance can help determine whether the activity and its intensity are suitable for their health and physical capabilities.

Could High-Intensity Exercise Help Prevent Osteoporosis?

The findings offer a new perspective on how exercise could be used to maintain bone health as people age. While the analysis focused on markers of bone metabolism rather than direct changes in bone density, the results suggest that vigorous activity may encourage early biological changes that support bone formation.

"According to the World Health Organization, regular physical activity offers numerous health benefits. However, our findings suggest that low-intensity exercise alone is not sufficient to stimulate bone metabolism. High-intensity exercise may trigger early beneficial changes in bone formation, potentially helping to slow bone loss and support healthy aging," summarized Dr. Nóra Sydó, clinical specialist and co-author of the study.

The researchers believe that understanding which movements most effectively stimulate bone formation could lead to better exercise programs designed to preserve skeletal strength and help prevent osteoporosis.

For now, the findings highlight an important distinction: staying physically active is beneficial for overall health, but keeping bones healthy over the long term may depend not only on how much people move, but also on how powerfully and dynamically they move.

Materials provided by Semmelweis University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4381. Petit Planet Preview: Living the Cozy Life

The latest major entry in HoYoverse's catalog sends us to distant planets. We explore the multiplayer mini-games and friendly neighbors and planet customizations at a recent event!

HoYoverse is well known for their free-to-play gacha experiences, telling surprisingly intricate stories all while compelling their player base to get their favorite characters. That looks to change in their latest entry, Petit Planet.

This is a big deviation from what we’ve become accustomed to when it comes to HoYoverse, as while aspects to the overall formula remain, a lot of it has been modified to accommodate a cozier experience. This is all about building a life on a small planet with all your friends, be them NPCs or those online.

We were invited out to talk to the developers a couple of weeks ago and play a newly updated build of Petit Planet, and we couldn’t have had a cozier experience.

Before getting into anything, it should be said how much more of a multiplayer game this is compared to any of the other HoYoverse games we’ve had in the past. Genshin Impact has multiplayer functionality, which somewhat carried into Honkai: Star Rail (which uses its events well for cooperative and competitive play), but Petit Planet looks to up it to another level.

This is supposed to resemble something like Animal Crossing, having players not only be able to visit each other, but interact with them to a great degree. You can send friend requests and then easily access their world, although the number of things to do there is contained. It’s going to the Grand Bazaar that really turns things up.

This is a social hub-like area where players can go and play games with one another. For example, there's a rhythm game four players compete in, along with an Uno type game. Each of these games have a maximum number of four players to utilize, although there are possibilities for more. Being that the game isn’t out, this likely will be the groundwork for even more mini-games to come.

Participating in this mini-games seem to give you a Jelly currency, which can then be exchanged from various vendors for emotes, some of which can be interacted with other players, and other articles of clothing.

Because this is a life sim, there will be several things to do in the world on a daily basis, especially given this is a free-to-play HoYoverse game. There are daily and weekly challenges that can be accomplished, from chopping down trees to interacting with the Neighbors, and each generate different types of currency.

Because this is a free-to-play experience, there are quite a few different curries you will be able to obtain through daily activities but of course spend with your hard-earned money. While this wasn’t in the build we had, there’s no denying that’s how the game will generate its income from. It will still allow players to do their daily and weekly activities to generate some of these currencies, ensuring you don’t have to swipe, but remember this is still a HoYoverse game at the end of the day.

As for what you’ll be able to participate in, there are various energy-spending activities, from gathering materials from around your world to catching bugs and sea life. All of this contributes to the overall progression, although we aren't entirely sure what the endgame will truly be.

This feels like a game where you can sit back and chill with friends, slowly building upon a world without much pressure or FOMO. Regardless, there are still things that can be done in the world to ensure for some sort of progression, but whether there's a true endgame is still up for debate.

This wouldn’t be a cozy game without NPCs that roam around the worlds, and Petit Planet has a bevy to see. We’ve already been introduced to a number of the cute and cuddly cast in the past, but there’s even more we got to see in the latest demo. Each neighbor has their own function for why they are in your world, but mainly it’s for you to build and expand upon the relationships.

The Neighbors come with their own progress tree, going up three levels and seemingly able to go down if you neglect them. You'll be able to bring them onto your planet and set up little houses for them, and that’s not all. They'll have their own stories and journeys to go through from meeting them, talking them over time and giving them gifts, unlocking various moments with them.

By obtaining Footprints and the other currencies in Petit Planet, you'll be able to exchange them for various in-game cosmetics, such as clothing, which include facial wear and full outfits, and various placeable items.

Making sure your home is homey is key to immersing yourself into the Petit Planet system, as there are numerous options to choose from when building your perfect little abode. Whether it’s the furniture, the appliances or simply the wallpaper, there’s a staggering number of customizable options.

On top of that, building out your planet itself is just as important, as setting up roads to your neighbors and modifying the different accessories are put around things such as gardens lets you do so much more. It’s your personal little place you want to call home, even though the chilly planet we got to play on is relatively small. Here’s hoping there’s ways to expand upon it.

Petit Planet will be out by the end of the year on December 4 for PC and Mobile devices, with a Nintendo Switch 2 launch sometime in 2027.
