#4302. 10 Open-World Games You Can Finish in 10 Hours & Under

Elena Chapella is a Writer for DualShockers. Previously an award-winning journalist, Elena is passionate about writing what she loves.

When any gamer hears about open world games, they immediately (safely) assume that the game would proceed to take hours upon hours to complete. However, that’s not always the case with open world games.

In fact, some of these games can be completed in less than 10 hours.

If you enjoy exploration-focused titles that are free of filler, we recommend the ten fastest open-world games to 100%.

For players who are wanting a one-and-done experience with an open world game, being able to beat it within the same day or two days maximum, these games scratch that itch. You’re able to hop in and complete the game practically quicker than you can download it, and it’s just the right amount of content to tide you over until the next game.

While others are diving into open world games to sink hundreds upon hundreds of hours into them, you can rest assured that these games won’t eat up your schedule.

The thing about Outer Wilds is that the world itself is the final boss, with players only having a limited amount of time in order to save the universe – but it’s not done on its own. The game’s DLC, Echoes of the Eye, is about 10 and half hours long, obviously shorter for faster players.

The DLC doesn’t replace anything in the game, but it’s rather a separate and self-contained location, more than ready for players to dive in and unravel its secrets. This way, if players are wanting a taste of Outer Wilds without going through the whole game, they can easily do so.

This is especially the case if you’ve already beaten the game/solved the mystery of the main story. Since there isn’t really any replayability, the DLC offers a whole new mystery altogether – in a way, it’s like you’re playing the game for the first time all over again, and it can be solved pretty quickly.

Thankfully, there are also even more DLCs if you want more mystery, but they aren’t anywhere near as condensed as Echoes of the Eye.

There’s something particularly special about Shadow of the Colossus: the game is labelled as an open world, but many players would walk away from it thinking that it’s a semi-open world due to just how empty the world itself is.

Of course, that’s typically a bad thing for open worlds, but the unique thing about Shadow of the Colossus is that it would not work without that emptiness. Combine this with a linear order for the bosses themselves (which are platforming puzzles as well), a vague yet compelling story and a genuinely cool premise, and you’ve got a game that’s as fun as it is challenging.

One of my students refers to the game as “Rated T for Teen Mario,” and I'm bound to agree, if that helps get the idea across. And just like Mario, the game can be beaten pretty quickly: about 7 hours, in fact.

With that in mind, if this is a game that interests you, be prepared to spend most of those 7 hours climbing rather than fighting; you’re going to love it regardless.

Right now, The Legend of Zelda once again has the gaming community in a complete buzz thanks to the fantastic reception to the Ocarina of Time Remake.

The series is continuously revolutionary, constantly evolving and redefining the open world genre as we know it. However, many tend to forget that open world Zelda didn’t start with Breath of the Wild, it started with the very first entry in the entire franchise.

The nice part about the game is that it’s not long at all (especially when compared to its sequels that will come over the next few decades) – averaging only at about 8 hours to beat the game. Players who want a traditional Zelda experience in a short amount of time can’t find any other game that would be a better fit.

And as the game comes up on its 40th anniversary, it’s all the more reason to dive into where it all began.

Obviously, both Red Dead Redemption games are massive, telling all kinds of stories jam-packed in a rich world of historical fiction, so it would take a while to beat either entry. However, the first game’s DLC, Undead Nightmare, is a fantastic stand-alone story that only takes about 6 and a half hours to complete.

Undead Nightmare takes everything you love about the classic Red Dead Redemption, but with a twist: suddenly, everyone is trying to survive a zombie apocalypse that came about practically overnight. The world and everything you can do within it, naturally, is related to this instead of your standard robberies and bounties.

Since the world is so condensed, the DLC goes by much quicker than most, but it’s an absolute blast from start to finish. In fact, it’s widely considered to be one of the greatest DLCs of all time, simply for how refreshingly unique and fun it is.

With that in mind, the fact that this game can be completed quicker than a standard work shift just makes it all the better.

Of all the Assassin's Creed games, the shortest mainline entry (non-DLC game) is easily Assassin's Creed: Rogue, clocking in at about 11 hours to be beaten (again, it’s much quicker than that for veteran AC fans and seasoned gamers as a whole).

Surprisingly, the game has one of the more unique stories that the series has seen, focusing on an Assassin named Shay Patrick Cormac literally going rogue, slaughtering the brotherhood he knows and siding with the Templars.

And the best part of the story is the fact that the modern-day segments are thankfully incredibly short – the segments that drag and feel like a chore in all the other titles in the franchise don’t bog down this game.

Overall, it’s the perfect bite-sized game for Assassin’s Creed content, regardless of if you’re a fan or even brand new to the series. It’s truly one of a kind, especially for a series like AC.

From the titans of Xenoblade to the lawns of Santa Destroy, these Wii open-world games prove curiosity always pays off if you’re willing to get lost.

If you were given 10 hours to simply explore New York City and soak it all in, you wouldn’t even be an eighth of the way through your journey before you reach that time. The fact that Marvel's Spider-Man brought in NYC on a similar (still scaled down) scale cemented the game’s timeframe as you continue to whip around as The Friendly Neighborhood himself.

Yet, you don’t have anywhere near as many superhero duties in Spider-Man: Miles Morales, so obviously, it will take you a lot less time. It would take about 8 hours, in fact.

Since you’re playing the game as Miles Morales (duh) while Peter Parker is still around and kicking, you’re basically a superhero in training. This training will have you busy constantly taking down bad guys and saving the day, serving as the sole Spider-Man in NYC for several hours until Peter comes back from vacation with MJ.

Or you could just swing around New York City doing whatever you want for that timeframe, you’d get the same amount of enjoyment.

Just because a game is a horror game doesn’t mean it can’t also be open world, and in DREDGE, our open world is a vast, dangerous ocean. Even then, it’s nowhere near as dangerous as it will be once your sanity drains due to the Lovecraftian terrors you’ll encounter.

It sounds horrifying, but it’s actually the coziest fishing game you’d ever imagine. You fish, fill out your encyclopedia, discover aberrations with the marine life and upgrade your ship, but the real fun comes from the simplest mechanic: sorting the fish into your boat. Seriously, the inventory management is the most addictive part of the whole game.

The nice part is that it’s wrapped up quickly, too, taking only about 9 and a half hours to complete – but trust me, you’re going to willingly sink far more hours into the game (and your ship). And if that doesn’t sound like enough content in the game for how much I sing its praises, it also has two equally dense and fun DLCs.

When it comes to short, yet full open world games, you cannot get any better of an experience than with DREDGE.

The lovely thing about Eastshade isn’t just how stunning of a game it is, but also the fact that it can be beaten pretty quickly and pretty easily – just around 9 hours.

The whole game is about finding the most beautiful spots in the game to paint them (using a photography mechanic), so those entire 9 hours are filled with genuine beauty. Of course, since it’s open world, there are side quests (artwork commissions) and other things to do, but you’re going to be far more caught up in how pretty the world is.

And for those who love subtle, environmental storytelling, this world is full of it. You can learn more while you’re out and about exploring in it, or from the various other characters that you can talk to.

It’s one of the few open world games that keeps you busy without actively stressing you out; since, after all, the point of the game is to relax you, you’re going to find yourself in a comfortable state of bliss while playing.

If you’ve ever wanted to feel like you’re driving a pod around Tatooine (like any Star Wars fan would), you would have a fantastic time with Sable.

The game seems pretty surface-level and simple: just ride around on your sand-speeder and enjoy the game’s lovely art style, but once you start playing, you’ll see it’s a lot deeper than you’d expect. It’s supposed to be about the protagonist’s self-discovery on their home planet, but by the end of your adventure, you’re going to feel like you’ve gone on a self-discovery of your own.

While the game can be completed in about 7 and a half hours, it’s actually better if you take your time with the exploration – that’s the game’s strongest component, after all. Why not take the time to enjoy a world as pretty and interesting as this one?

It’s not perfectly polished; it’s actually pretty janky of a game at times, but if anything, it makes you love the game and all the charm it has even more. At the same time, if some of the previously mentioned jank (charm) is a little too much, then rest assured that you can get through this game very, very quickly.

A Short Hike is just that: short. It’s not the kind of short where it’s on the shorter end of a long game, no, the game is only about an hour and a half long. If you try to complete every single element within it to 100% the game, you’re looking at about 4 hours, an incredibly tiny open world game.

The premise of the game is simple: you’re hiking up a mountain. If you run into anyone or anything on the way there, you’re more than welcome to interact with them, but it’s optional if you’re wanting to just get to the top. Considering how short the game is, I’d recommend not skipping anything if you can help it, just to get the richest experience you can.

Don’t rush through this hike, either. The game is already short enough, and there is so much enjoyable content that you don’t want to miss out on while on the way to the top.

But as we’ve learned with games like these: it’s not about the destination, it’s about the journey, so don’t be afraid to go on that journey.

#4301. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with... a questionable selection of maps, but at least the modes are good

If Redsec got you hooked on Battlefield gameplay but you never experienced traditional multiplayer in Battlefield 6, there's an upcoming moment you might want to pay attention to.

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

This is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

The Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

Instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two new maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

As for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

Beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two new maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

The miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for new players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

#4299. Battlefield 6 streamlines some of the most annoying Challenges yet again, takes out a few of them entirely

The easier and more accessible Battlefield Studios makes those Battlefield 6 Challenges, the better.

The work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a new patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

The Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

The journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The issue encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing new Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently announced that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

#4298. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

#4297. Arc Raiders patch nerfs the Deadline mine, ends the menace of the Venator

The first post-Stella Montis patch for Arc Raiders has arrived, and it predictably touches much of what people brought to the latest map.

Arc Raiders has received a new update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the new “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s update, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

The patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

Check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. You should also learn what all the different Map Conditions do in Arc Raiders, and how to best make use of each of them.

#4295. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

#4293. Treyarch Lays Off Call of Duty Zombies Mastermind Craig Houston After 20 Years

Contributor at DualShockers, former Esports Insider DACH content lead, former Escapist Magazine Germany content lead, software engineering background.

Craig Houston, the writer behind much of Call of Duty’s Zombies storyline, has been laid off by Treyarch after around 20 years at the studio.

As the development of Black Ops 7 winds down, Treyarch has indicated that they'll make big changes to Zombies in their future Call of Duty games.

He shared the news himself on Friday via X and LinkedIn, and I have to say, it’s a rather graceful message considering the circumstances. Houston said he was proud and privileged to have worked alongside so many talented people, many of whom will remain friends for life, before thanking fans for their enthusiasm, support and kind words over the years. On X, he posted it alongside a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch, featuring footage from many of the games he worked on, which makes the whole thing feel a little more bittersweet.

He didn’t go into the reasons, but it appears to be part of the huge Xbox restructuring announced earlier this year, which is set to affect 3,200 jobs. Treyarch sits under Activision Blizzard, which in turn is owned by Xbox, so it isn’t a huge surprise that the cuts have reached the studio. Still, seeing a name like his on the list stings, especially if you’ve spent any amount of time shooting zombies with your friends at 2 in the morning.

For those who don’t know him by name, and I suspect that’s quite a few people, Houston has been at Treyarch since 2006. His first Call of Duty there was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor, which is a pretty humble start for someone who would go on to shape one of the series’ biggest modes. From World at War in 2008 onwards, he was the main writer for Zombies, whilst also writing for Treyarch’s campaigns.

He is credited as a writer and designer on Black Ops 1 through 4, and later as part of the design and creative development teams on the likes of Cold War, Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7. Interestingly, he isn’t credited on this year’s Modern Warfare 4.

Zombies obviously wasn’t a one-man show, with Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell and Kevin Drew all being a big part of how the mode evolved. Houston’s writing is what a lot of fans point to when they talk about why they fell in love with the characters, though. He also wrote the jingles for the original perks introduced in Verrückt, which is one of my favourite details in all of this. If you’ve ever caught yourself singing along to a vending machine whilst a horde closes in on you, that one’s on him.

The response since Friday has been lovely to see. Former Treyarch developer Tony Flame replied to Houston’s post calling him a legend and saying it was an honour to work with him, adding that he created a truly special experience that will live on for millions of fans. Over on Reddit, one fan described him as a great guy, noting that you can tell how much he loves the story and characters he writes simply by how excited he gets when talking about them in promo material.

Many fans argue that Houston never quite got the recognition he deserved. In the wake of this announcement, many people admitted they hadn’t really been aware of him until after Black Ops 3, despite him having been there since the very beginning, and I think that’s true for a lot of us players. We tend to know the directors and the faces from the trailers, whilst the people writing the lines we end up quoting for years stay in the background. Zombies a mode spawned out of passion, and it’s hard to see someone fundamentally involved with that leave.

Truth be told, this is the part of the Xbox restructuring that I find hardest to get my head around. Twenty years of knowing a story inside out, including every timeline, every character and every twist, isn’t something a studio can simply hire back in. Of course, I don’t know the reasoning behind this particular decision, and Houston himself hasn’t said a bad word about Treyarch. It is, however, a reminder that these layoff numbers are made up of people, some of whom have been shaping the games we love for the last two decades.

Houston hasn’t said what he plans to do next. Whatever it ends up being, I hope it involves writing, and ideally a jingle or two.

#4292. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

Gen.G beat LYON 3-0 in Allen, Texas, removing North America's last team from Worlds 2026. The LCK top seed are now one series from a first Worlds final, with a revived Invictus Gaming in the way.

Gen.G swept LYON in the second Worlds 2026 quarter-final in Allen, Texas. The defeat removes North America’s last team from the tournament. The LCK top seed now face Invictus Gaming in a best-of-five semi-final on Saturday, starting at 16:00 Central Time.

Reaching the last four secures Gen.G at least third or fourth place. That is a familiar stopping point for the organisation. It has finished third or fourth at four of its last five Worlds and has never played in a Worlds final, GosuGamers reported.

The stakes go beyond one team. Gen.G entered the tournament as the LCK’s top seed. Korean sides are chasing a fifth Summoner’s Cup in a row.

Their opponents bring their own history. Invictus Gaming beat Top Esports 3-1 in the opening quarter-final. That put iG into their first Worlds semi-final since 2019. TheShy and Rookie, who won Worlds with iG in 2018, are back in the last four.

The money rises sharply from here. Worlds 2026 carries a US$5,000,000 prize pool. The champion takes US$1,000,000 (20%), and the runner-up receives US$800,000.

For LYON, the exit still marks clear progress. They go out in joint fifth to eighth place and collect a share of the prize money. GosuGamers called it easily the organisation’s best Worlds finish. In four earlier appearances, LYON never placed higher than 17th.

Their elimination also changes the shape of the event. North America will have no representative in the semi-finals or the Grand Final. The remaining matches in Allen will be contested without a team from the region.

LYON are eliminated from #Worlds2026. pic.twitter.com/y5cWOL9e5K

The Grand Final is listed for 14:00 EST on 14 November. British fans will have a dedicated place to watch it. The British Esports Federation is holding a watch party at the new British Arena in Sunderland. It is the venue’s first esports watch party.

The arena covers 15,000 sq ft. It has a 17-metre-wide LED screen, a 200-seat viewing area and a bar. Students can get discounted tickets.

Whether Gen.G or iG make it to that final will be settled in Allen on Saturday. The Sunderland watch party runs from 5:30pm on the day of the final until 1:00am on 15 November.

The Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this new chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

All is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

The highly-anticipated Durin is at last the new playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. #4287. Battlefield 6 kicks off its first free trial post the Black Ops 7 launch to twist that knife

Activision has done its own fair share of Battlefield 6 counterprogramming prior to that game's release, and EA is here to repay the favour with Black Ops 7.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

The trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

Players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

It's not surprising that the devs have changes in mind following so much public feedback, though it is a little surprising that it will take until sometime next year for those adjustments to be complete.

#4283. The latest Arc Raiders patch is almost entirely about fixing exploits, including all the clipping through locked rooms business

Embark is clearly sick of Arc Raiders players exploiting the game's mechanics to push each other around, and clip through doors and walls.

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of new fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

The list of notes for update 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

This fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an issue whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

The game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

#4282. Assassin’s Creed Franchise Update Reveals Codename Hexe News Coming Next Year, New Game Plus for Valhalla, And Confirms No New Remakes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

This news comes a few days after New Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”

As for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First announced in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing update on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories.”

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases big celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. "

For more on Assassin's Creed, check out our review of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

#4280. 10 Survival Games That Don’t Make Hunger Their Whole Personality

Contributor at DualShockers, former Esports Insider DACH content lead, former Escapist Magazine Germany content lead, software engineering background.

Survival games have had a hold on me for years now. There’s truly nothing like crash-landing somewhere hostile with nothing but the clothes on your back, punching a tree, and slowly building something that resembles a home. What I could absolutely do without, though, is the little drumstick icon that starts flashing at me roughly ten minutes into every new world.

From Rain World's terrifying sights to Subnautica's oceanic survival, these are the 10 Best Open World Survival Games.

Look, I get it. Hunger is realistic, and in some games, it genuinely adds to the experience. But far too often, it feels like a chore that’s been bolted on because that’s just what survival games do, and I’m not being funny, but I didn’t plan an entire expedition just to turn around because my character fancies a snack.

Thankfully, not every developer feels the same way. Some have turned food into a reward rather than a punishment, some have made hunger completely optional, and a few have decided that your character doesn’t need to eat at all. They’re all still survival games, and some of them are pretty brutal, so let’s take a look at my favourites that found far more interesting ways to try and kill you.

Valheim is pretty much the poster child for survival games that do food differently. There’s no hunger meter, and you will never starve to death, no matter how long you go without eating. Instead, you can have up to three different foods active at once, with each of them boosting your maximum health and stamina before slowly wearing off.

Skipping a meal won’t hurt you, but it will leave you with a measly 25 health and 50 stamina, healing a single hit point every ten seconds. Considering a single troll can flatten you in a matter of seconds, that’s more than enough motivation to get cooking. Food becomes part of your preparation, just like repairing your gear before a big boss fight, rather than something you need to do just to stay alive.

Note: Iron Gate reworked the entire food system with the Hearth & Home update back in 2021, and truth be told, not everyone was thrilled about it at the time.

After more than five years in Early Access and over 17 million copies sold, Valheim finally hit 1.0 on 9 September 2026, together with the Deep North biome. Eating is still optional. Heading into the Mistlands on an empty stomach, however, is a mistake you’ll only make once.

Keen Games, the Frankfurt studio behind Portal Knights, didn’t exactly hide where its inspiration came from. Ahead of Early Access, the team said that Enshrouded would have no hunger meter, no thirst meter and no sleep meter, and that Valheim was the closest comparison for how food would work. And honestly? It shows, in the best possible way.

Food in Enshrouded is all about buffs. You get three food slots, and only one food of each type can be active at a time, which nudges you towards mixing and matching rather than just shovelling roasted meat into your mouth. Some meals boost your health, others your melee or magic damage, and it ends up feeling much more like putting together an RPG build than ticking off a survival chore.

Note: About six months into Early Access, Keen Games added an optional Survival difficulty that brings the hunger bar back. On that setting, it can actually kill you.

I think that’s the perfect compromise. If you want the classic experience, it’s there for you, but if you don’t, you’ll never have to think about it. More than five million players had already wandered into Embervale before the 1.0 release on 15 October 2026, so I’m clearly not the only one who appreciates that.

Terraria has never had a hunger meter. Sure, food exists, but it gives you the Well Fed buff, a lovely little boost to your stats rather than something standing between you and certain death. You can spend hundreds of hours digging, building and taking down bosses without ever having to think about lunch.

That changed, sort of, with the 1.4.3 update. Re-Logic teamed up with Klei Entertainment for a crossover with Don’t Starve Together, and the result was The Constant, a secret world seed that brings in hunger, Don’t Starve-style shading and darkness that actively hurts you. Hunger works in stages, and if you ignore it for long enough, you will start starving.

Note: The whole crossover started with a Reddit AMA for Terraria’s 10th anniversary, where the team said Don’t Starve Together was the franchise they’d most like to collaborate with. Klei just so happened to be reading.

I absolutely love this approach. Nobody is forced into it, but it’s there as an opt-in challenge for anyone who wants it. The fact that you need to type in a secret seed to even get hunger tells you everything you need to know about how essential it is to the Terraria experience.

Players will need to be extra careful when exploring in these open-world and survival games.

Astroneer has a pretty simple take on survival: you need oxygen, and that’s about it. Your shelter provides you with both power and oxygen, so as long as you stay within range, you’re absolutely fine. The moment you wander off, though, your meter starts to drop, which is where tethers come in to carry that oxygen with you.

What I love is how that one mechanic shapes everything else. Your tether lines double as breadcrumbs, so you always have a way back home, and the tension only really kicks in when you’re deep in a cave and very much off the grid. It’s survival with all of the tension and none of the snack breaks, and that’s exactly why I keep going back to it.

System Era Softworks released Astroneer into Early Access in December 2016, before launching the full game in February 2019. Sadly, co-founder and lead artist Paul Pepera passed away in March 2017, before the game was finished. His distinctive low-poly style still defines Astroneer to this day, and by March 2022, the game had been purchased nearly four million times.

No Man’s Sky doesn’t have a hunger meter, a thirst meter or anything that even resembles sleep. What it does have is life support and hazard protection, and both of those need topping up whilst you explore planets that are, more often than not, actively trying to kill you. Some players will argue those are just hunger and thirst with different names, and fair enough, but in practice it feels completely different.

You’re not foraging for berries. You’re mining oxygen and sodium, refining resources and keeping your exosuit running whilst dodging toxic rain or extreme temperatures. Instead of pulling you away from exploring, your survival is tied directly into it.

Food did eventually find its way into the game with a full cooking system, letting you turn ingredients into dishes that restore life support or hazard protection. There’s even a food critic, Cronus, who will rate your culinary creations and reward you with nanites. It’s completely optional, slightly absurd and exactly the kind of thing No Man’s Sky does best.

Subnautica does have hunger and thirst in its default Survival mode, so this one comes with a little asterisk. When you start a new game, though, you can pick Freedom mode instead, which is identical to Survival, just without hunger and thirst. You’ll still have to manage your oxygen, your health and your nerves, and trust me, that is more than enough.

Plenty of players recommend Freedom as the best way to experience Subnautica for the first time, and I’d have to agree. Inventory space is already tight, and every slot you don’t fill with fish is a slot you can use for resources. That way, you can fully focus on exploring the oceans of planet 4546B, which are, quite frankly, terrifying enough on their own.

Note: Freedom mode isn’t a late addition, either. It has been there almost from the start, and PC Gamer’s preview in January 2015, just weeks into Early Access, already listed it alongside Survival.

Unknown Worlds launched the full game on 23 January 2018, celebrating with a livestream from the Monterey Bay Aquarium. By then, nearly two million people already owned it. Considering what lurks in the deeper parts of Subnautica, I personally would’ve picked a slightly less fishy location.

These games are sure to keep fans of the Subnautica series entertained.

Satisfactory is a factory-building game first and a survival game a very distant second, but it still drops you onto an alien planet full of wildlife that would love nothing more than to take a bite out of you. What it doesn’t do is make you eat. Food is purely there to heal you, and the planet’s edible flora are more like a first aid kit than an actual meal.

Paleberries heal 10 HP, Beryl Nuts a little less, and the Bacon Agaric mushroom heals 20. Eventually, you can even process them into inhalers, because of course the answer to everything in Satisfactory is automation. The only real hunger in this game is your factory’s endless appetite for more power, more iron and more conveyor belts.

Note: ADA, your ever-so-helpful AI companion, refers to the Bacon Agaric as Amanita Lardum. Whether it actually tastes like bacon remains a mystery.

Coffee Stain Studios released Satisfactory 1.0 on 10 September 2024, after over five years in Early Access and 5.5 million copies sold. And the big reveal in the release date trailer? A flushable toilet. We all have our priorities.

Starbound, Chucklefish’s sci-fi sandbox, lets you decide on your relationship with food right at character creation. Casual mode removes the need to eat entirely, Survival mode adds a hunger meter, and Hardcore combines hunger with permadeath for anyone who enjoys suffering. There’s no switching later on, so you’d better know what you want before you start.

Interestingly, hunger had actually been taken out during development, and was only brought back for the 1.0 release on 22 July 2016, specifically for the Survival and Hardcore modes. In those, food rots over time, and you will starve if you ignore it. In Casual, food still heals you and grants buffs, so cooking never feels pointless.

I really appreciate a game that respects the fact that some of us just want to build a pretty space station and go planet-hopping in peace. Not every adventure needs a ration plan. Starbound can still be pretty challenging in other ways, but in Casual mode, the biggest threat on a new planet is the local wildlife, not your rumbling stomach.

There are so many great co-op games coming out today, and many allow players to just explore and relax together.

Pacific Drive is a survival game where you don’t need to eat, drink or sleep. Instead, almost all of the survival pressure lands squarely on your station wagon. You patch up panels, swap out tyres, keep the battery charged and the tank full, all whilst driving through the bizarre, anomaly-filled Olympic Exclusion Zone.

Seth Rosen, who led the game’s design, has been pretty open about the fact that a lot of his choices were aimed at smoothing out the things that bugged him about survival games. He even had pages of notes on turning radiation damage into an exposure meter, but ultimately decided against it, since you already have your hands full taking care of the car without another time pressure and distraction. As Rosen put it, the car’s health is generally a better indicator of how a run is going than your own.

Note: Creative director and CEO Cassandra Dracott’s 1989 Buick Estate was the primary reference car during early development. Her parents’ Volvo station wagon, which became the car she drove from the moment she could drive, played a part, too.

Ironwood Studios released Pacific Drive on 22 February 2024, and it sold over a million copies within a year. There’s even a television adaptation in development, and I truly have no idea how they’re planning to make a car the main character. I cannot wait to find out.

LEGO Fortnite launched on 7 December 2023 with a fairly traditional hunger system. You could already switch it off when creating a world, but for anyone who kept it on, it wasn’t exactly a great time. Within two weeks, Epic patched it to make snacks more filling, because food simply wasn’t reducing hunger by enough. In hindsight, it was the first sign that hunger and LEGO minifigures weren’t the most natural pairing.

In mid-2024, Epic added Cozy mode, which turned hunger, temperature and stamina off by default. That should’ve been the end of it, but Epic eventually went one step further and removed hunger from Odyssey altogether. Food and potions still exist and give you buffs, but there’s no meter to keep topped up anymore.

Note: Not everyone was happy about it, with some players saying the change made the game feel a little too arcade-like.

Personally, I think it was the right call for a game that lives inside Fortnite and attracts plenty of younger and newer players. Odyssey is all about building villages, exploring and fighting off the occasional Storm-Wild creature. Nobody needed to stop every few minutes to hunt down yet another LEGO berry.

These survival games are the best to come back to and explore to your heart's content solo or with friends time and time again.

#4279. The MongolZ end FURIA’s winning run as NAVI send Falcons out of IEM Beijing

The MongolZ beat world No.1 FURIA to reach the IEM Beijing semi-finals, while NAVI eliminated big-spending Falcons in the group stage. The results reshape the picture of the main contenders before the PGL Major Singapore opens on 24 November.

Against world No.1 FURIA on Wednesday, The MongolZ recovered after dropping the opening map. MOUZ have also booked a semi-final place after going unbeaten in Group B.

The defeat ended a seven-game winning run for FURIA, HLTV said, although the match was not an elimination game. FURIA had not lost since winning PGL Masters Bucharest. They now face BetBoom in the quarter-finals.

The second map, Cache, was FURIA’s own pick, and The MongolZ had lost on that map in each of their previous four attempts. This time they won it, then closed out the series on the third map.

The timing gives the result extra weight. IEM Beijing is ESL’s top-tier CS2 event and the last big tournament before the Major. FURIA are still alive, but the series shows they can be beaten by the sides around them.

Falcons went out in the Group A lower-bracket final. NAVI recovered from a narrow loss on the opening map and dominated the rest of the series. On the Mirage decider, NAVI won all 12 rounds of their T-side half.

w0nderful went 25-4 on Inferno. b1t then took over on Mirage.

For a big-spending organisation, an exit before the playoffs is a setback. Falcons share seventh to eighth place with Team Liquid, and the two teams earn the same amount. That compares with $360,000 for the champions.

Liquid also fell at the final hurdle. BetBoom beat them 2-1 to take the last playoff place in Group B. A zorte ace in round 23 of the Mirage decider swung the series. PARIVISION, who finished behind MOUZ in Group B, meet NAVI in the other quarter-final.

The $1,250,000 prize pool is split into $300,000 in player prize money and $950,000 in club share. The event is being played at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena in Beijing. It is listed as an ESL Pro Tour Masters event.

The playoffs are single-elimination best-of-three series. A best-of-three third-place match will also be played, and the grand final is best-of-five.

#4278. Battlefield Labs is coming back for a short session to test out next week's Battlefield 6 update, and you can expect more tests in the future, too

Battlefield Labs is evolving, as it reopens its doors for its next - unusual - session.

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season update not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

The December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Battlefield Studios announced a host of new changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an issue that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

The patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios says should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Going forward, Battlefield Studios said to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect new maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

#4277. Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek, X-Men, And Myriad Video Games Actor, Passes Away

According to a report from The Hollywood Reporter, actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86. Stewart spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared that he died after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”

Stewart was best known for his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation (and its various spinoffs) and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but he did plenty of video game performing, too. Stewart played Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, one of the first characters you meet in the game, and Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He also played Jean-Luc Picard in about 10 different Star Trek games and Charles Xavier in five different X-Men games.

Stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment. Jean-Luc Picard will undoubtedly be an enduring and important character in the Star Trek franchise, and that's thanks to Stewart's portrayal of the starship captain. His portrayal of Charles Xavier also helped to legitimize the comic book movie, and he will appear again as the character in this year's upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.

Our thoughts are with his friends and family, and the millions of fans (of which I include myself) who are mourning his loss. Let's all drink some Earl Grey tea in his honor today.

#4276. Honkai: Star Rail 3.8 will run for an extra two weeks while Version 4.0 is in the oven

The next Honkai: Star Rail update is upon us, and there's a mix of good - and unusual news.

HoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major update. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also announced that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

This final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

#4275. Attack on Titan Revolution tier list - pick your family

A full explanation of what AoTR families represent and ranking them according to their power on the Attack on Titan Revolution tier list.

This tier list is focused solely on the families. There are a total of 28 families you can play, and one Secret family (Shiki), which cannot be obtained at the moment. We've not added that to the list, so don't worry about it too much. Instead, we are going to dive deeper into the other families and why we've ranked them the way we have.

Of course, there are different rarities, but it doesn't always mean that the rarer a family is, the higher it will rank. So buckle up, because if you're new to the game, you need to learn which ones you should be keeping!

How to get new families in Attack on Titan Revolution There is only one way to get families in Attack on Titan Revolution, and that is by using your Spins for a chance to get one of the top-tier options. If you want more Spins, check out our list of Attack on Titan Revolution codes, because we have collected all of them, and they can give you a nice advantage for free.

After performing 400 spins, you get a guaranteed family of Epic or Legendary rarity - so keep spinning!

Now that you have a better understanding of the AoT Revolution families, let's dive into the actual Attack on Titan Revolution tier list! S Tier  |  A Tier  |  B Tier  |  C Tier  |  D Tier

Ackerman This ability is one of the best in the game, and if you followed the anime/manga Attack on Titan, you know it's based on Captain Levi Ackerman. It's undefeated in terms of the amount of damage it dishes out.

Yeager As the name implies, this family is the one Eren Yeager was part of. This one revolves around gaining certain stats while in Titan mode, as well as regeneration. If you like the playstyle, it's an amazing family to obtain.

Reiss The Reiss name is one that Historia Reiss bears in the anime/manga, as the name of "Krista" at first. As you can imagine, just from the name alone, you can tell they are strong. In AoT Revolution, the Reiss family name bears a similar resemblance and brings about a few interesting perks, such as controlling Titans.

Tybur The Tybur family is a great family for grinding. It grants increased Gold gain and has enough Regen to let you solo instances, even if you have a good enough setup. It's Epic, but it is heavily reliant on Titan.

Leonhart The Leonhart family is one of the only two Epic families landing in the S tier in our Attack on Titan Revolution game tier list. That's because although it doesn't have a lot of extra skills, the stats it grants are outstanding, and with the Shifter Regen skill (the only skill it grants), it's got amazing synergy.

And that's our complete Attack on Titan Revolution tier list of families ranked according to their overall power. Since you love Roblox games so much, we can recommend checking out our World of Stands tier list and One Fruit tier list as well.

#4274. Tomorrow’s Battlefield 6 patch is the first step towards improving footstep audio, and it might actually fix the settings reset bug

The next major Battlefield 6 patch is nearly upon us, and Battlefield Studios is promising a bounty of changes - including a couple of fixes to some big bugs.

Battlefield 6 is about to receive a new update. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the new patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

The Ice Climbing Axe is the only new weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Easily the most interesting change in this update is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this update is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy issues with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the issue should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.

#4272. Death Stranding Isolations Animated Series Gets New Teaser Trailer

A new teaser trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an upcoming animated series coming exclusively to Disney+ and Hulu next year, premiered during Kojima Productions’ 10th Anniversary Exhibition Beyond the Strand. The series was first announced last year.

Death Stranding Isolations tells an original story in the Death Stranding universe set immediately after the events of the first game. Isolations is created by Japanese animation studio E&H Production (Ninja Kamui, Bullet/Bullet, Magic Knight Rayerath) and directed by Takayuki Sano.  Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima serves as executive producer.

Today’s teaser video provides the following story synopsis:

The Death Stranding—a catastrophic series of explosions caused when the dead crept into our world and collided with the living.

In the wake of this cataclysm, many were forced to live in absolute isolation—among them, a young girl. Although this lonely existence was forced upon her, she soon grows to prefer solitude, eschewing all opportunities for real human connection and allowing herself to be strung along by fate.

In Death Stranding, legendary game creator Hideo Kojima brought you a haunting vision of a shattered world. Now, that world expands into new frontiers with a brand-new animation series.

Under the guidance of director Takayuki Sano, world-class hand-drawn animations have been brought to life by renowned studio “E&H production” (NINJA KAMUI, BULLET/BULLET, the Magic Knight Rayearth television series).

The story is set in North America immediately after Sam—the protagonist of the game—reconnects the continent by means of the Chiral Network. However, as America is reborn from the ashes, the renewed connections that bind it together bring about new and unforeseen consequences.

In this tumultuous new landscape, there are some who walk a different path to the one chosen by Sam and his Bridges comrades: a wise old man who connects people through a method that defies all reckoning; a female soldier ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction; a boy who seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life...and of course, the girl who chose to sever all ties with the outside world...Fate has other plans for her, however, and chance encounters see her launched headfirst into a world she does not recognize.

Death Stranding Isolations is coming to Disney+ and Hulu in 2027. It’s one of the three planned big-screen adaptations of the series. An animated movie called Death Stranding: Mosquito (working title) is also in the works alongside a live-action Death Stranding film by A24.

For more on Death Stranding, check out our reviews for the first game and its 2025 sequel. You can also read the latest update on Kojima Productions’ upcoming stealth-espionage game, Physint.

#4271. Battlefield 6's latest update dubbed the game's simultaneously best and worst patch as it runs into all kinds of issues

What's likely going to be the last major Battlefield 6 update of the year has launched with a number of unexpected issues.

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.
