#4270. 10 Games That Made Me Weirdly Passionate About Jobs I'd Never Want

Contributor at DualShockers, former Esports Insider DACH content lead, former Escapist Magazine Germany content lead, software engineering background.

Some of my favourite games are, when you really think about it, just jobs. I have pressure-washed patios, stamped passports, hauled cargo across half of Europe and sold second-hand books out of a trailer, all of it voluntarily and in my free time. And boy, did I take every single one of them seriously!

The Best Cozy Games That You Need to Play in Fall 2026 feature autumnal settings and the distinctive vibes of the season.

The funny thing is that I wouldn't actually want any of these jobs. Some of them look like far too much hard work, others require a kind of patience I most definitely do not possess, and with one or two, I'm fairly certain I'd end up in prison. That is probably exactly what makes them so enjoyable from the safety of my sofa, so let's take a look at the ten games that made me weirdly passionate about jobs I'd never want.

I had sunk many hours into both PowerWash Simulator games long before I ever held an actual pressure washer. That finally changed earlier this year, and I'm pleased to report that watching grime disappear is just as satisfying in real life as it is on screen. On a warm summer's day, it's even quite fun.

Still, there's a lot to be said for staying warm, dry and cozied up on the sofa whilst doing it. The game has an almost meditative quality that I couldn't quite find with a real hose in my hands, and that's no accident. Lead designer Nick McCarthy has said that the team left out certain real-world inconveniences on purpose, and I'm grateful for every single one of them.

FuturLab released the sequel on 23 October 2025, bringing 38 new jobs to Muckingham, online co-op for up to four players and new tools like an abseiling rig and a cherry picker. There are also two kittens named Bubbles and Squeak, which was frankly all the convincing I needed. As an actual career, though, it looks like an awful lot of work, so I'll stick to the version without the wet socks.

Papers, Please's premise is incredibly dark and difficult: you are manning a booth at the border of the fictional Eastern Bloc country of Arstotzka. It's 1982, and as a border inspector, it is your responsibility to check passports, permits and anything else that gets slid across your desk. Make a mistake and you get a wage deduction. Your family, meanwhile, desperately needs that money. The game is, however, also tense and brilliant, and it also taught me that I would be entirely unsuited for the job.

Quite frankly, I'm just not enough of a bootlicker for it. I'm far too nice, and my first instinct is to wave everybody through, which is not something Papers, Please looks kindly upon. Being generous with your stamp sooner or later gets you killed by your own government, and it's hard to build a career on that.

Note: Lucas Pope worked on the Uncharted series at Naughty Dog before making a game that's almost entirely about paperwork.

By its tenth anniversary in 2023, the game had sold over five million copies, so there are clearly plenty of people out there who are much better at saying no than I am. I have a lot of respect for them. I'd just rather not meet them at passport control.

Running a late-night coffee shop in an alternative version of Seattle sounds like a dream. Even more so when you consider that your visitors will consist of elves, orcs and mermaids that are living alongside humans. Coffee is the great connector here, since the need for a warm drink and someone to talk to is universal across every race. Toge Productions chose Seattle because Starbucks first opened there, and also because the rain sets the mood so well. It's easily one of the coziest games I own.

Parts of this job would actually suit me extremely well: I enjoy good banter, I'm perfectly happy with small talk, and I seem to have the kind of approachable face that makes strangers trauma dump on me far more often than you'd expect. If being a barista was only about listening, I'd be employee of the month.

Unfortunately, you also have to make the coffee, and Coffee Talk is the game that showed me just how hilariously bad I am at latte art. Nothing I produce looks like it was made on purpose. So as much as I love the idea, I could never run a coffee shop of my own.

Note: Creator Mohammad Fahmi sadly passed away in March 2022. He pitched the game as holding a warm cup of coffee by a window whilst it rains outside and lo-fi music plays in the background, which is exactly how it feels.

If you're looking for relaxing experiences with guaranteed quality, I recommend these ten little-known cozy games from famous developers.

Stardew Valley is meant to be about running a cute little farm with cute little animals on it. The way I play it, with spreadsheets at the ready and more wiki tabs open than I'd like to admit, has very little to do with that. My approach is a lot closer to a general planning a war than a farmer enjoying the countryside.

The forensic intensity I bring to this game does scare me a little. Every day is planned, every crop has to earn its place, and my poor character hasn't had a quiet afternoon in years. If I ran a real farm like that, I'd work myself into a burnout before the first harvest.

Note: Eric Barone, better known as ConcernedApe, made Stardew Valley on his own over roughly four years.

The game turned ten on 26 February 2026 and has sold around 50 million copies. I'd love to know how many of those players are peacefully watering their parsnips and enjoying the sunset, and how many are like me. I have my suspicions.

Something happens to me whenever I open Euro Truck Simulator 2. Within minutes, I turn into a 60-year-old trucker who has been doing this for decades, completely locked in, with nothing on my mind except my cargo and the motorway ahead. I can't explain it, but it awakens something in me.

There are two wolves inside of me: One is a sweet softie, and the other one is a fourth-generation trucker that graduated from the school of hard knocks, living and breathing 18-wheelers. Sadly for the second wolf, I'm really, really bad at parking, and truth be told, I'm no better at it in the game. That feels like a bit of a dealbreaker for a job that ends with reversing a trailer into a loading bay.

SCS Software first released the game at retail in autumn 2012, before it arrived on Steam on 16 January 2013. By its tenth birthday, it had sold over 13 million copies, and players had bought DLC more than 80 million times. Clearly, I'm not the only one with a trucker wolf, so at least I'm in good company.

Exterminauts is an upcoming co-op shooter from Behaviour Interactive, the studio behind Dead by Daylight, and it hands you several jobs at once. As part of a crew of three, you clock in, take on MegaCorp contracts, repair what's broken and exterminate alien pests along the way. It was revealed at gamescom Opening Night Live in August 2026 and is planned for 2027.

Anyone who has watched me deal with a woodlouse or a spider knows that pest control isn't my calling. I'm quite a caring person, so I had a lot of fun with the healing side of things. I've also discovered that I'm alarmingly quick to shoot my own teammates, sometimes because they were being annoying, and sometimes entirely by accident.

Note: Friendly fire is on in Exterminauts, and swinging one of the bigger weapons around carelessly is enough to take a teammate down.

A colleague who keeps taking out the rest of the crew isn't much use to anyone, no matter how good her healing is. I can't imagine it going down well in a performance review, either. It's better for everyone if I stay off the payroll.

Subnautica is one of my favourite games of all time, which means I approach the deep ocean with a healthy dose of suspicion. Dave the Diver has done nothing but confirm that this is the correct attitude. You spend your days diving into the Blue Hole to catch fish, and the further down you go, the more things would like to eat you instead.

Once the sun sets, the second job begins, and you help chef Bancho run the sushi restaurant, serving customers and keeping the drinks coming. All of that after a full day of nearly being eaten by sharks! I’d be a horrible sushi tester on the basis of not liking fish, and I could also never be the waiter on the basis of lacking a good sense of balance.

Note: The restaurant is the idea of Dave's friend Cobra, a former arms dealer who now handles the business side of things. Naturally.

By September 2026, Dave the Diver had sold more than 10 million copies across all platforms, and I completely understand why. It's a wonderful game. It's also the best argument I've ever seen for staying on dry land and ordering takeaway.

A review of over the hill, a cozy exploration-focused driving game.

Kerbal Space Program puts you in charge of a space program run by the Kerbals, little green aliens who are far braver than they have any right to be. You build rockets, launch them and watch most of them explode. I was oddly passionate about all of it, right up until the moment I finally made it into orbit.

I'm very aware that the game doesn't end there. It had taken me so long to reach that one milestone, though, that my passion fizzled out on the spot, and I decided that my work here was done. That's quite unusual for me, as I'm normally someone who needs to tick off every last goal.

A real head of a space program with that attitude wouldn't bode well for anyone. NASA worked with developer Squad on an asteroid mission update in 2014, and ESA followed with missions of its own in 2020, so the people who do this for a living are clearly made of sterner stuff than I am. I have a lot of respect for them, and I'm more than happy to watch from the ground.

Barbie Rewind was developed by Digital Eclipse, published by Atari and released on 12 November 2026. It is unfathomably fun. You get to decorate the DreamHouse with over 250 pieces of furniture and decor inspired by real Barbie playsets, from a classic pink vanity to a '90s inflatable chair. There are also 16 classic Barbie games from 1991 to 2007 included, one of which, Barbie: Vacation Adventure, had never been released before.

Truth be told, I think I'd make a good interior designer, and I think I'd enjoy it, too. In Barbie Rewind, you get to design to your heart's content, and nobody questions your choices. Ken, Teresa and Christie do pop in to ask for help, but none of them will ever tell you that your sofa is ugly.

Real clients are a different story. Even when something looks questionable at best, you have to go with the flow and keep them happy, and whilst you'd hope they trust your design decisions, there's absolutely no guarantee that they will. I don't think I have the temperament for that, and I'm fairly sure someone would end up wounded.

In Tiny Bookshop, you leave everything behind to sell second-hand books out of a little trailer in the seaside town of Bookstonbury-by-the-Sea. Each morning, you pick a spot, stock your shelves and wait for the locals to wander in. Many of the books are real ones, which I love.

I've worked in retail before, I'm quite a good salesperson, and I enjoy helping people find what they're looking for. The customers in Tiny Bookshop put that to the test, because a fair few of them behave as if it's their very first day on Earth. Not all of them, mind you, but enough of them describe the book they want so vaguely that it borders on nonsensical.

On top of that, everyone in town seems to need a favour. Community is important, of course, but I'm trying to run a bookshop here, and I'd quite like to be left alone to do it! Over half a million players have fallen in love with Tiny Bookshop, and it won three German Developer Awards in 2025, so this one might just be a me problem. I'd still end up scaring all of my customers away.

#4268. EA Reportedly Closed BioWare To Invest In Developing Star Wars Battlefront III Instead Of The Next Mass Effect

Electronic Arts shut down the legendary RPG studio BioWare last week, ending development on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game. Since then, we've seen what appears to be a leaked trailer for the game, which suggests it might have been called Mass Effect Universe, and heard a sneak peek at what Grammy-winning composer Austin Wintory was cooking up for the beloved sci-fi RPG series. Over the past week, fans across the internet have tried to piece together how a publisher could decide to shut down a studio as prolific as BioWare, but according to a new Bloomberg report, the answer is Star Wars.

More specifically, Bloomberg writes that, presented with the opportunity to develop Star Wars Battlefront III with Disney, the publisher, which went private last year after a $55 billion acquisition,  chose to invest its money into that instead of BioWare's in-development Mass Effect sequel. The publication writes that EA looked at its portfolio for the coming years and had two massive sci-fi investments it could continue: Star Wars Battlefront III or BioWare's next Mass Effect. Even though Mass Effect was well into development, and even though the Battlefront threequel hasn't even entered development, EA chose to continue with the latter. And so BioWare was shut down, and Mass Effect development ended, though Bloomberg's sources say there are other, less significant reasons the studio was shuttered, too.

Those other factors include the poor reception to 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda, the failure of Anthem in 2019, and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which, despite garnering positive critical reception, apparently missed EA's sales expectations by 50%.

There's also the uncomfortable reality that BioWare made progressive LGBTQIA+ positive games but was a studio within a publisher house now partially owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a government fund from a country where same-sex activity, including marriage, is criminalized, sometimes punishable by death; these harsh laws extend to other facets of the LGBTQIA+ community. Another investment partner in this acquisition of EA is Affinity Partners, a Miami-based investment firm founded and run by former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, a political figure who imposes laws that discriminate against the LGBTQIA+ community, especially the 1% of Americans who are transgender; Trump has also been known to mock this community in various ways. No official statements say BioWare shut down because of its progressive leanings, but one has to wonder if that was a factor, especially after reports that BioWare scrubbed diversity from demos to avoid negative feedback from EA (thanks, Kotaku).

When BioWare closed last week, only 50 employees remained, all working on the next Mass Effect, after years of layoffs at the studio.

A Mass Effect TV series is still in the works at Amazon, even though EA seems to have hung up Commander Shepard's video game suit for good.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4264. Aurora Gaming sweep Pixel Lumina to reach Europe Qualifier 1 final after BONK disqualification

Aurora Gaming beat Pixel Lumina 2-0 to reach the Europe Qualifier 1 final, days after the UK side that had knocked them out was disqualified for cheating. The final decides seeding for the Europe Qualifier Playoffs, the next step towards VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027 in Berlin.

Aurora Gaming will play in the Europe Qualifier 1 final. Their best-of-three semi-final against Pixel Lumina began at 16:00 on Tuesday. Aurora took the opening map in 41 minutes and closed out the second in 35 minutes.

The win completes a turnaround for a side that had already been eliminated from the qualifier. Their earlier exit had come against BONK.

The fallout reached beyond the bracket. Every BONK player and registered participant was also provisionally suspended, GINX TV reported.

The disqualification forced a rework of the schedule. Riot had set Qualifier 1 for 5 to 8 November as a single-elimination, best-of-three bracket. The Pixel Lumina semi-final and the final were pushed back to make room for the rebuilt bracket. All three affected organisations agreed to the new timetable.

Pixel Lumina, a team based in Hungary, came into the match at rank 120 in the Elo power rankings. They hold a rating of 1559 and a 30-28 record across 58 rated matches. Aurora are unranked. Before this semi-final, Pixel Lumina lost to CGN Esports in the VCL EMEA Last Chance Qualifier 2026. That defeat followed wins over FOKUS and Twisted Saints Esports in the same event.

Aurora’s lineup features Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx. Derke joined straight after Valorant Champions 2026, where his Vitality side lost the grand final 3-1 to LOUD.

Aurora now face the winner of xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx versus F9 EICAR. That final decides seeding for the Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs. Aurora are already listed as qualified for the playoffs through Qualifier 1, so the final is about position rather than survival.

— Aurora Valorant (@Aurora_Valorant) November 10, 2026

The wider prize is a place at VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027. Europe will supply half of the four non-partner sides heading to the event, Riot Games said, while Türkiye and MENA each send a single team. Kickoff itself will be played offline at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin with 12 teams.

The rest of the European field is still taking shape. Europe Qualifier 2 is scheduled for 12 to 15 November and is also played as single-elimination best-of-three brackets.

#4263. Elemental Powers Tycoon: Complete Powers tier list

Have you recently started playing Elemental Powers Tycoon and are unsure which powers are the best? Well, you’re in luck because our Elemental Powers Tycoon tier list will assist you in figuring this out. We have rated all powers from S to D, with S being the highest and D the lowest. This tier list lets you focus on mastering powerful characters and avoid struggling with the lower-tier options. We've added a description for each character to help you understand the reasoning behind their ranking.

Elemental Powers Tycoon is an enjoyable Roblox game that draws inspiration from various anime, merging the typical tycoon format with powers acquired using money. The developers made the skins of their characters resemble famous figures from many anime series and movies, including Naruto, One Piece, and HxH.

Additionally, I’ll be incorporating numerous anime references. If I’ve overlooked any anime or characters, please let me know in the comments.

Now, let’s jump straight to the tier list.

Thunder Thunder is among the super-broken characters in EPT and sports a Killua-like appearance. It’s understandable why it’s OP; it has an exciting and all-around kit with damage and a long-duration stun. Even though you can fly around on Nimbus like Goku, there’s no Kamehameha. Instead, you have a flashy and strong thunder attack that can one-shot almost everyone, which is sufficient to rank the character at the top of our Elemental Powers Tycoon tier list. Time This character can stop time and slow down enemies, holding an exciting kit of skills and well-balanced damage. He is among the most OP champs, although the S-tier rank is for the excellent invisibility skill. You can go unnoticed by your adversary for a short time, making for a comeback moment in every fight if used strategically. If you are into time manipulation and want to become the invisible man, here’s your chance. Nature Hashirama is the master of nature manipulation, an influential figure from the Naruto series. In the game, he is famous for his wood and tree attacks. One of his skills is the ability to pull any enemy in a specific direction, which you can use to drag them into your deadly attack range. I also consider the damage high, which makes him easily qualified for the S tier. Technology Now we have my favourite character, and you will understand why once you try technology. He has the best skill kit with high damage output. The sword he holds can throw projectiles every third strike with no cooldown, and he can summon two large hexagon-shaped cells that fire towards the cursor’s position. But these are not the only perks! You can summon a turret that knocks enemies around, levitates, and becomes invulnerable to damage while being able to cast skills. And finally, create a tesseract that sucks in anyone approaching it to deal 63 damage over nine pulses. This character is your best pick if you want to dominate EPT easily. Bones Bones is another OP champ, well-known for having almost average skill damage, but that one “jealousy” skill that can one-shot everyone sets the bar high to be in the S tier. I would recommend it for those who want to abuse one skill and get the most out of their kills.

Darkness2024-03-05 Darkness is powerful right now. If you’re a Madara Uchiha wannabe, you will enjoy this pick. The kit resembles purple shadows and the special Giant Hand move that pulls opponents underneath. Catching someone in it is an inevitable knockout. There’s also the ability to teleport forward for a surprising attack or to dodge enemy overkill skills. Overall, darkness is considered strong, but it is not the best choice. The downside is that it’s hard to hit your main skill, which makes winning a gamble. Light Light is Admiral Kisaru from One Piece. All fans of the series will recognise them instantly. The character has a fantastic set of skills and abilities. You can run fast, teleport, and damage your enemies significantly. Remember that high mobility is necessary in this game, and people who can master this character will also be hard to kill. Space Space, represented by an astronaut’s skin, is an above-average character with a mix of solid and weak weapons. However, it made it easy to reach the A tier thanks to the UFO skill and the significant damage some of his guns inflict. Another downside is his melee weapon, which is not the best to swing around. Devil Denji represents the devil from the Chainsaw Man series. Boasting above-average skills made it easy to get into the A-tier list. The damage and the mobility skills are well-balanced. The character mainly focuses on wielding a devil sword that deals hellfire damage over three cycles, teleporting in the cursor's direction, inflicting damage upon landing, and throwing puddles of black fluid as projectiles. Devil is very entertaining and strong at the same time. However, why not in the S tier? The answer is simple: I’m considering how tough it is the land some skills. Venom Venom is a toxic character, as the name implies. He uses poison, which deals continuous damage and empowers attacks. He holds a stun ability, self-buff (health and speed) and bubbling venom, which covers a wide area. The character is a good choice, with many players already invested in mastering him. The melee damage could be better, and is the only downside of this character.

Ice Ice, a character as cold as Esdeath, has the most exciting skill in their stun, which limits the enemy's mobility and jump power. It is super-efficient against high-mobility tycoons. However, it does come without a downside. The skill set doesn’t hit hard for overkill, and she lacks burst damage, making her a laid-back character requiring patience. She is undoubtedly the best pick if you’re into that play style, however. Gravity Admiral Issho represents gravity from One Piece, but this time, the character is in the okay-ish category. It has some good stuff and skills, but remains in the B tier if we talk about the best powers, as other Tycoons could easily overpower it. The other downside is his firepower hitbox, which is hard to land and needs to be more dominant on the battlefield. Crystal We place Crystal in the B category, the epitome of average characters, because her kill options aren’t as deadly as they should be, making it a bit hard to deal with enemies. The more you play her, the more you discover how challenging she is to use. Supersonic Supersonic is all about speed and hitting from a distance. His moves include Sonic Blaster for ranged damage, Sonic Barrage for a quick burst of projectiles, and Sonic Twister to zip around the map. He’s a great pick if you like fast, agile play rather than relying on raw power or heavy crowd control.

Fire Fire is somewhat useless, as sadly represented by Naruto, but it has one of the best skins in the game. The number of combos you must do to defeat someone is tremendously annoying. I wouldn't recommend this character if you are seriously trying to beat some enemies. It's only a good choice if you're entirely into aesthetics.

Earth Earth is low because you have to be lucky to hit your skills. It’s hard to use since the hitboxes are small and your range is short, so you must get close to your opponent. Even if you miraculously land some hits, they won’t be deadly enough to eliminate your adversary, which is annoying. It's not my cup of tea, but feel free to try him out.

That’s all for our Elemental Powers Tycoon tier list. I hope it is helpful for all the newbies and veterans alike. I'll update it accordingly as the meta changes, which it surely will. Until then, have fun and keep an eye on similar content like our Anime Dimensions tier list, Blade Ball ability tier list and Ultimate Tower Defense tier list.

#4261. The Top 10 Best Horror Games To Play This Halloween

Humans are drawn to horror in all forms, real life and fiction. Perhaps it’s the desire to get as close to death as possible without actually dying; perhaps it’s the morality of life and knowing death comes for all of us; perhaps all our heads are just a little miswired. Whatever the reason, we flock to movies where supernatural entities and puppets on tricycles upend otherwise lovely lives, TV shows where murderous cults kill and stump local detectives, and books where the words on the page seem to follow you to bed. Games, however, go a step further, letting you enter the horror and control it (or become its victim), and you could argue that, as a result, they’re the most immersive form of fiction.

We at Game Informer love a healthy dose of horror from time to time, and we often review games like this. Some terrify us. Others… don’t. And the best ones stick with us for years and years after the credits. Below is a list of 10 of the best horror games we’ve played recently. This isn’t an all-time list, so don’t fret if your personal favorite isn’t here. Instead, this is a collection of 10 horror games ordered by release date that we think are great for spooky season and beyond. Let us know in the comments what you would add to the list!

The cozy corner of the horror genre seems to have exploded overnight, and now tons of new slice-of-life horror games are in various stages of development. That said, the team behind newcomer The Village in the Shade is no stranger to the form; they made the Yomawari series, a cute-and-terrifying collection of creepy virtual tales. The Village in the Shade takes things back to the homestead, giving you (a child who emerged from a hole in the ground and was immediately given the responsibility of running an entire farm by yourself) the freedom to plant, sow, reap, ranch, and more. Just follow the important rules: don't go out at night, don't share secrets, and don't leave the village among others. You wouldn't want to break the rules, right? You could, theoretically, go about your idyllic rural living. But as you unravel the threads of what this village is, who you are, and why you're here, it's hard not to get drawn into the strange, mysterious, delightfully disturbing truths hiding in its shadows. Just don't forget to water your turnips before you go sneaking out again.

Fans of survival horror and old-school FMV adventure games will find plenty to love (and fear) in Tenebris Somnia. When a young woman visits her ex-boyfriend’s apartment and discovers he's trapped in a hellish dream world, it kicks off a well-executed survival-horror trek of inventive puzzles and resource management to overcome dangerous monsters. High-production, live-action cutscenes help tell the story of a deteriorating relationship and the toll an indie horror film took on its creators, and they play an important role in gameplay. Tenebris Somnia may not look like much due to its classic pixelated presentation, but its scares and story captivate. – Our Review

Resident Evil Requiem is not just one of the best Resident Evil games, but it’s also one of the best horror games ever made. It features a unique dual-protagonist structure. Grace Ashcroft is timid, new to the whole “shooting zombies in the head while dealing with Umbrella viruses” thing, and is generally just trying to do her job. Leon S. Kennedy, however, is a veteran of all that and more. Requiem splits its runtime between the two characters, letting you experience both sides of Capcom’s marquee survival-horror style. Grace’s sections leave your hands clammy and your blood pressure high as you desperately try to survive. Leon’s sections leave your hands shaking with adrenaline and your blood pumping with excitement as he mows down zombies (sometimes literally, courtesy of those pesky chainsaws). The result is a Resident Evil game that blends two typical RE experiences – terrifying and tough or exhilarating over-the-top action – into one cohesive package. It’s perfect for someone who wants to feel scared and then soon after receive the catharsis of being the one in control, like being the tragic victim who dies in Act One of the horror movie and the last one standing who lives to tell the tale. – Our Review

Little Nightmares developer Tarsier Studios has a knack for delivering creepy side-scrolling adventures, but Reanimal eschews any whimsy to become its scariest game yet. While mechanically it is similar to Little Nightmares and still puts small children in unimaginable peril, Reanimal is capital-H horror thanks largely to its terrifying threats and disturbing animal-themed imagery (this probably isn’t the game for animal lovers; some messed-up stuff happens to these critters). Escaping the game’s island setting is thrilling and chilling whether you’re playing alone or with a friend in co-op. Months after release, we’re still thinking about Reanimal’s memorable final sequence, which is worth the price of admission on its own. – Our Review

2001’s Silent Hill 2 is considered one of the best horror video games of all time for good reason. At release, it was a graphical powerhouse, using the PlayStation 2's horsepower to create a setting that begged to be explored, even though every bone in your body said you shouldn’t. The remake from developer Bloober Team took on a big task in modernizing the game without losing the original’s soul, and it did a great job. Among all the recent Silent Hill releases (Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall), the remake is our favorite. The story of James Sunderland and his troubling relationship with his departed wife is complex, emotional, and – important for the purposes of this list – unsettling and scary. – Our Review

Alan Wake 2 is an excellent pick for some spooky madness, in the vein of David Lynch’s seminal Twin Peaks mystery-surrealist series. Don’t worry too much about the “2” part of the game’s title. You just need to know that the titular Alan Wake character is a not-great writer who acts like he’s really great, his wife is missing, and he got trapped in the ambiguous Dark Place. He’s only one half of the Alan Wake 2 equation, with his segments set in a dream-like version of New York City. Playing as him feels the most Twin Peaks-y. The other half is Saga, a police officer who arrives in the Pacific Northwest town of Bright Falls to investigate a murder that might be linked to a cult. You can expect more traditional survival-horror gameplay from her. But this is still a Remedy Entertainment game, and without spoiling anything, it goes places. And along the way, you can expect plenty of scares. Turn the lights down low (or off), light a candle, and sit back and enjoy one of Remedy’s best games. – Our Review

Square Enix has gone two-for-two with its Paranormasight series, an anthology of stories about the strange and occult. And while the more recent Mermaid's Curse is a brilliant tale all its own, the first entry – The Seven Mysteries of Honjo – brings significantly more scares. A group of people in the city of Honjo find themselves caught in a spectral battle royale, using powerful objects and conditions to curse one another, with the allure of a prize at the end. Its magic isn't just in the flowchart timeline, where you can hop between different perspectives and protagonists to see how events play out from every angle, but also in the gorgeous stereoscopic environments and narrative puzzles. Adventure games are a classic genre, and Paranormasight will remind you of what the genre is capable of the moment you slowly spin your camera around, your eyes peeking out from behind your fingers.

Survival horror can contain multitudes, and as the years have worn on, the genre has grown to encompass a wide range of action-combat mechanics. Signalis feels like a re-centering in that respect. It's an isometric survival-horror indie project from developer rose-engine, filled with clever puzzles, scarce resources, limited inventory slots, and looming, oppressive dread. As the Replika unit Elster, you delve deep into a remote complex filled with horrors and monsters, searching for something, or someone, waiting down below. While love for classic horror games and other hallmarks of genre fiction will certainly draw you in, the stylish presentation and devastatingly human core will keep you forging ahead to the finale. Once you've breached the surface of Signalis' retro-future super-structures, you won't be able to turn back.

In horror movies, audiences often groan at a protagonist for putting themselves in seemingly grave danger just to learn more about a cursed amulet or bloodthirsty killer. But in Immortality, you are the protagonist, and despite a lingering sense that you shouldn't be digging into the archives of these abandoned films, each eerie new scene makes you want to dive deeper. It's a game about Marisa Marcel, an actress who almost starred in three movies in the late 20th century, but has since disappeared. None of the movies were ever released due to mysterious circumstances, but you have access to the archived, unedited live-action footage, including behind-the-scenes conversations. By scrubbing through footage, you can select people or items in each scene and jump to random footage from any other movie that includes the same person or item. The approach to puzzle-solving is unique and keeps you appropriately disoriented. The mystery at the center is an unsettling treat to unravel, and scary in new and unexpected ways. Immortality is one of a kind and an easy recommendation for horror fans who want to try something a little different.

In the decade since launch, Dead by Daylight has continued to succeed, thanks to a dedicated (and newcomer-friendly) fanbase and its towering roster of original and licensed personas from across pop culture horror. The asymmetrical multiplayer title has become an anthology of horror’s biggest faces, including Freddy Krueger, Ghostface, Pyramid Head, and even the Xenomorph. Whether you play as a Survivor, trying to escape all manner of nightmare locations through stealth and cunning, or as a Killer, whose experience feels more like a hunting club, you’ll understand why Dead by Daylight has become a recurring destination for fans of the gruesome and bizarre.

Read about the making of Dead by Daylight and how it sunk its teeth into millions of players in our six-page exclusive feature in Issue 368 (p. 42), available in our magazine archive to anyone with a free Game Informer account.

#4260. Reinstated Aurora Gaming beat F9 EICAR to win Valorant Europe Qualifier 1

Aurora Gaming came from a map down to beat F9 EICAR 2-1 and win the first VCT EMEA Kickoff Europe open qualifier. The win came days after they were put back into the bracket when the UK team BONK was disqualified for cheating.

The VCT EMEA Kickoff: Europe Qualifier 2027 decider got under way at 18:45. The series began on Lotus. Aurora’s chiwa was named most valuable player of the series.

The Aurora roster lists Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx. F9 EICAR, based in France, fielded Kipperman, Destrian, Tenshi, izana and Geekkooo.

Aurora’s run nearly ended early. BONK, a UK Valorant roster, beat them 2-1 in the round of 32 on 6 November. That result followed a comeback from 3-11 down on Bind. Riot’s ruling against BONK reversed Aurora’s exit. Every BONK player and registered team member was provisionally suspended. Project 100K and ycatble returned to the bracket along with Aurora.

The qualifier left no room for error. It was a single-elimination bracket for 256 teams, and every match was a best-of-three. Once reinstated, Aurora did not drop a map before the final. They beat Pixel Lumina 2-0 in the second semi-final.

In the first semi-final, xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx fell 2-1 to F9 EICAR. The French side had arrived at the qualifier in mixed form. F9 EICAR lost 0-2 to WIP Esports in VCL France: Revolution Stage 2 2026 and were twice beaten 1-2 by Mandatory. A 2-1 result against Esprit Shōnen was their only victory in that run.

The Elo power rankings show the gap on paper. F9 EICAR sit at rank 241, with a rating of 1405 and a 6-16 record in 22 rated matches. Aurora are unranked.

The final still carried weight. Seeding for the playoff stage would be decided by the result, Insider Gaming reported.

The playoffs will use a modified double-elimination bracket of best-of-three matches, with a best-of-five grand final. The top two finishers earn places at VCT 2027 EMEA Kickoff, whose window runs from 14 January to 7 February.

#4259. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. You can count on one hand the days that remain until the launch of GTA 6. Players will finally be able to embark on a new crime-ridden narrative with dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia. With launch events on the horizon, it has been revealed that Twitch will be joining the action.

A GTA 6 launch celebration will take place on the online streaming platform, Twitch. It allows players to snag GTA 6 rewards to use on their profiles and when chatting in their favorite streams during the game’s launch week and beyond.

12.5 million American gamers plan to adjust their schedules for Rockstar's next big release.

Twitch leaked this campaign themselves, detailing all the rewards up for grabs. It has since been deleted, but thanks to Insider Gaming, we know all that the GTA 6 Twitch drops will entail ahead of time.

As part of the campaign, you can unlock six viewership Bling Badges by watching GTA 6 streamers for one hour each day on six different days between November 18 and November 30, 2026.

Although GTA 6 launches worldwide on November 19, the Twitch drops going live a day early are likely because streamers and fans alike will be doing the New Zealand trick in order to get access to the game as soon as possible.

The six Bling Badges available to collect depict a chain with “VI” as the charm, beginning with a purple chain, then bronze, silver, gold, diamond, and finally, the Miami chain, which is covered in the iconic GTA 6 purple, pink, and orange hue.

The Twitch drops going live a day early is likely because streamers and fans alike will be doing the New Zealand trick

They aren’t the traditional Twitch drops fans hope to see from games, as they usually involve items you can equip in-game, such as cosmetics. It’s unlikely that you will need to link your Rockstar account to Twitch because only Twitch items are up for grabs. If you want to prepare for any potential future drops, you can connect your accounts by going to the Rockstar Games website and logging in, selecting the profile icon to go to your account and settings, and finding linked accounts and connections to authorize a Twitch account connection.

If you’re trying to avoid story spoilers, GTA 6 streams probably aren’t the place to be, but it depends on how badly you want the badges and emotes. You could always leave a stream running in the background for an hour while you explore Leonida yourself.

#4257. Creatures of Sonaria tier list of all creatures

In this peculiar Creatures of Sonaria tier list, we'll guide you through all of the creatures and explain which ones are worth keeping.

Would you like me to also pull together a top 10 current meta creatures list so you can see where Idrabark and Deluumar sit compared to the absolute best?

We bet you have probably heard of Creatures of Sonaria if you're a fan of Roblox games. It has become very popular.

Creatures of Sonaria throws you into a fantasy world with mythical beasts, most of which are harmless to the environment. But these mysterious creatures include some bloodthirsty predators who seek to kill you.

To defend yourself from your enemies, you need to know which creatures are worth levelling up to be your guardians. Want to know which ones deserve your attention? Then you should take a look at our Creatures of Sonaria tier list.

We have creatures ranked based on their highest potential. The information provided in this guide is for guidance only and in no way restricts your choice.

At the very top of this Creatures of Sonaria tier list, you can find the most powerful creatures with practically no weaknesses. They take less time to train, as they are less demanding in terms of equipment. Creatures Turrim, Vielheart, Goreganthus, Khu'Vuk, Taburúún, Boreal Warden, Celeritas, Gobli, Crata Peretina, Gnolrok, Gramoss, Gyroudus Norrok, Morthorax ,Hellion Warden, Hygos, Kendyll, Lmakosauruodon, Lus-Adarch, Sar’Hingaro, Iztajuatl Gimon-Ogu, Scrimpeii, Sigmatox, Syroudon, Nolumoth, Yeba’idi, Brequewk, Pterolythux, Felikxtrox, Pliarys, Exotide, Shiziyou

Notes on Boreal Warden The Boreal Warden is a terrestrial herbivore that was once available during Winter Events 2021-2022. The creature itself is mysterious and rare, making it very hard to find in Sonaria. These giants are rather passive, helping neighbouring herbivores who are looking for protection. Notes on Gramoss Gramoss is a terrestrial herbivore. This species is available in the Herbivore gacha. Gramoss is an obedient and sociable herbivore, capable of empathising with other creatures. It can often be seen sheltering small creatures under its body as they graze in search of food. Gramoss's body shape is similar to that of Koryser. It has small wings, which it is unable to use for flight. Its design and name may be a reference to gargoyles covered in moss. Notes on Lmakosauruodon Lmakosauruodon is a herbivore that lives on the ground. You can obtain it in the Herbivore Gacha. It looks like a sauropod dinosaur. It has a beetle-like crest on the end of its nose and many spines on its neck. Its colours are turquoise, brown, and yellow.

The creatures on this list are very strong and have one incredibly strong or several strong sides. Creatures Gorvulith, Mycenlich, Grimcorr, Dioxikin, Vespritte, Korathos, Fyranili, Cimidstik, Imini, Aolenus, Haechionx, Archalium, Ardor Warden, Moemoea, Nyctoxon, Polymonstrum, Qurugosk Zoltraack, Muravil, Arsonos, Axothan, Boskurro, Buff Eulopii, Sturbi, Chamei, Yggdragstyx, Zeoarex, Cryptoth, Gryvila, Fleuralis, Salrahn, Umbraxi Embristiss , Capukoralu, Pentagloss , Exterreri, Imeaorn, Opralegion, Dieamarjla, Jotunhel, Kohikii, Laharpes, Luxsces, Lerachu, Lure, Magnarothus, Militrua, Heisoteri Plumetik, Avothius, Sana’ata, Turgeon, Ura, Novus Warden, Kavouradis, Varskela, Venatrox, Verdant Warden, Verklixin, Nakamaska, Vetemortem, Yohsog, Slaiorn, Meorlark Arachyu, Zethines, Verza, Wewuix, Hyboria, Dalghara, Cavengauu, Aleicuda, Erridea, Empiterium, Flipli, Lactarim

Notes on Buff Eulopii Buff Eulopii is a terrestrial herbivore. This species is no longer available in the gacha. It was obtainable during the Easter Event 2021 by fighting the Buff Eulopii boss.

It was later returned during the Easter Event 2022 as a random drop from the Scrambler boss.

Buff Eulopii is similar to Eulopii. The main differences between the two are that the Eulopii Buff looks larger, bipedal, more muscular, and has a broad torso and abs. Notes on Polymonstrum This is a terrestrial herbivore. This species is available in the Herbivore Gacha. These tall beauties are friendly. If they ally with other herbivores, they take good care of the animal's life. Their horns reach the foliage high up on the trees, thus making noise. This helps to scare away any living creatures in the trees so that others will not eat them. Notes on Sana'ata Sana'ata is a terrestrial carnivore. The species is only available in the Rotation Store. When it comes to Sana'ata, they are spoken of as slow and very bulky creatures, found mostly near minerals or caves. They have pickaxe-like limbs over their shoulders, as well as a pickaxe-like outgrowth on the end of their tail. They are used for both combat and mining.

In this section of the CoS tier list, we have the creatures that are a great option for a newbie. Most of them have special abilities.

Notes on Knalriki Knalriki is a terrestrial omnivore. The species is available in the Session gacha. Since Knalriki are small, they are nimble and very fond of food. They can often be found gathering around carcasses in the hope of getting full.

Knalriki are long-limbed creatures with spines running along parts of their bodies and scorpion-like barbs on the end of their long, thin tails. Their heads are slender and converge to a point, though they have no eyes and have numerous teeth that protrude from their mouths even when closed. Notes on Therolachus The Therolachus is a semi-aquatic herbivore. The species is available in the Herbivores gacha and the Semi-Aquatic gacha. Therolachus resembles a hippopotamus with slender legs. Behaviour-wise, the Therolachus is similar to a rhinoceros or hippopotamus. They live in groups of up to 10 to 12 individuals, usually led by an alpha male. They are effective both on land and in water. If you are suddenly chased by this creature, do not worry that it will follow you for a long time, as they do not go far beyond their territory.

B tier includes simple creatures that can help in battles, but require a lot more time and effort to do so. As with the A tier, it may take longer for them to become stronger.

Notes on Diokrine Diokrine is a terrestrial photocarnivore. This species was obtainable in a Limited gacha but is no longer available in any of them. The Diokrine is a green theropod with features similar to the dinosaur Dilophosaurus, featuring foliage ruffles and a head crest with a bright blue underside. These beasts are always hungry and searching for food. They are nimble, fast, and intelligent. But despite the above information, the creature is weak and unlikely to help you all that much.

These creatures have to be given maximum attention if you want to get great combat performance out of them. It's wise to limit using them for the most part.

Notes on Pero Pero is a flying omnivore. The species is available in the Omnivores gacha and the Sky gacha. The Pero has a bird-like body form with a tiny beak-less face. There are two rows of glowing lights on its neck and tail, eight in total. Pero is a feathered bird with remarkable flight ability. As Pero grows, they have light bulbs that let them become invisible and hide from predators. CONCLUSION Our Creatures of Sonaria tier list is not the be-all and end-all. A properly grown and used C-tier creature can be just as effective as an S-tier one in a number of situations. It just sometimes takes more effort to get them there. We hope you found this CoS tier list useful and that you can now start training those at the top. We have covered a lot of different Roblox games, so you can also find a Anime Dimensions Simulator tier list, My Hero Ultra Impact tier list and a reroll guide for most of them.

#4256. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4255. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

#4254. Angel Legion tier list - Pick the right girls for your team

To make the most effective team, you'll need the most powerful heroes, and this Angel Legion tier list sorts them all out so you don't have to!

Updated on November 16th, 2026 - Version: 85.1 - Latest Addition: Lunar Saintess - Wangshu

The best heroes you can use in Angel Legion have outstanding skills that you will want to use from the very beginning. You can't always get the S-tier options from the get-go, of course, but ideally, you want to try summoning as often as you can (using the free daily summon as well) so you can try to put together a strong team.

I believe you can make most of the heroes work, as long as they have a decent synergy. Angel Legion is not that punishing in that regard, as long as your heroes are upgraded, they're quite capable. However, in the later stages, having a hero who is at the top of our Angel Legion tier list is going to make beating each stage a lot simpler.

Miya is the MC of Angel Legion, and the hero you first customise once you start playing. She can be viable regardless of loadout, since she can be pretty tanky, a good buffer, and a good damage dealer, all packed together into one hero.

Magic Arrow is an outstanding damage dealer who can fit in anywhere. She can cast her active skill quite a lot, and she can buff the energy of her entire column. If you pair her with a hero who can stun, you have a very strong combo on your hands.

Sakura Dancer is one of the best healers in Angel Legion. She can remove debuffs from her team, making her a good hero to have on your team regardless of the content you try to clear, be it PvE or PvP.

Dragon Knight is able to do AoE hits, making her exceptional for clearing PvE. She is a good hero to invest in since she can help you clear content all the way through until the end game. However, she's in the S tier because she is easily countered in PvP, but for PvE, she is a god.

Joan of Arc is a tank, and a really good one, too. She can boost the healing she receives, allowing her to tank for days, and can also mitigate some of the damage taken by her team.

Vera, although she looks like Jinx (of League of Legends and Arcane fame), is a hero to look out for. She is great at sealing ST damage, and can also stun the enemy she is attacking.

Oda Hime is a decent damage dealer, since she has a pretty good AoE skill. She can debuff enemies, preventing them from gaining Energy.

Rin Matsuzaka is a healer and a really good buffer. She needs a lot of dodge, since she will also buff the team's dodge. She can easily be replaced by a higher-tier healer though, so that's why she is only A-tier.

Avila can deal damage and debuff enemies. She can reduce the enemy's damage RES, and together with her AoE attacks, she can be a pretty reliable hero to have on your team.

Agraia could have been better had she only focused on one trait - right now, she wants to be a tank and a DPS, but is not good at either. She can be okay in the early game until you get something better, but otherwise, don't bother with her.

Hestia focuses on damage over time, but sadly, it is not that good. She is just disappointing.

Anna is an okay-ish unit, but sadly, she can't fit well into many teams. You should go for a different hero straight up, rather than trying to fit her in somewhere.

I do not recommend investing too many of your resources in these heroes. The probability of getting someone in one of the higher tiers is pretty high, and you will only end up wasting resources if you focus on them. So, try to swap them out the first chance you get with someone from the top of our Angel Legion tier list.

In my honest opinion, I think rerolling is quite tedious, and since you have several ways of upgrading your heroes, it's not necessary. However, if you really want to reroll, you need to prepare a second or maybe even a third account to link to. That's why I believe it is not worth rerolling at all in the first place.

These are all of the heroes in Angel Legion, ranked. For similar guides, take a look at ourHeaven Burns Red tier list and Girls Frontline 2 Exilium tier list.

#4253. T1 brings TenZ out of retirement a day after re-signing crashies from Fnatic

T1 has added two-time Masters champion Tyson 'TenZ' Ngo to its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. The move ends his retirement and builds on T1's signing of crashies, who has just left London-based Fnatic.

T1 has ended Tyson ‘TenZ’ Ngo’s retirement. The organisation confirmed on 12 November that he will join its Valorant roster for VCT Pacific in 2027. It made the announcement with a post and a welcome video.

T1 called him a ‘living legend’ of Valorant. It said he was starting a new chapter with the organisation.

TenZ retired from professional play in 2024. He has spent this year at T1 as a content creator. The announcement moves him from that role into the competitive squad.

His record explains the attention. With Sentinels, he beat Fnatic 3-0 in the Masters Reykjavík 2021 final. He then won Masters Madrid 2024 with a 3-2 win over Gen.G. That made him the first Americas player to win more than one VCT Masters event, Liquipedia records.

The TenZ news came a day after T1 confirmed Austin ‘crashies’ Roberts. He returns six years after T1 released him in September 2020. crashies called T1 the place ‘where it all started’. He said he was excited for the new challenge.

He played for Fnatic from 11 December 2024 until 4 November 2026. He joined T1 on 11 November 2026.

His exit is part of a wider reshuffle at the London-based organisation. Fnatic lost the Masters Toronto 2025 grand final 3-1 to Paper Rex. It then lost the Valorant Champions 2025 grand final in Paris 3-2 to NRG. On 2 November, Fnatic released head coach Andrey ‘ENGH’ Sholokhov. It said it was making changes ahead of the 2027 season.

T1 has also kept some continuity. It extended BuZz’s contract on 6 November 2026. The new deal runs until the end of 2028.

The VCT structure for 2027 was announced on 28 October. Under it, the eight Pacific partner teams go straight into Kickoff in January 2027. The other four Kickoff places go to teams from regional open qualifiers.

#4252. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4249. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.
